01:world-as-gods-house.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:world-as-gods-house.label: The world as God's house
01:world-as-gods-house.def: The whole cosmos is built as God's dwelling; heaven is His finished throne-house and earth is meant to become one.
01:world-as-gods-house.christ: Heaven, “…”, is progressively pressed onto His people as the house is built (ch. 4, p. 51).

01:highest-heaven.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:highest-heaven.label: Highest (third) heaven
01:highest-heaven.def: The heaven of Gen 1:1, made before the earth: God's throne-house where the angels live, invisible to us and the pattern for everything below.

01:heaven-earth-axis.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:heaven-earth-axis.label: Heaven as blueprint for earth
01:heaven-earth-axis.def: A vertical axis on which heaven is the archetype and earth the copy, so earthly order is modelled on heaven's pattern.
01:heaven-earth-axis.texts: Gen 1:1; Matt 6:10; Exod 25:40; Heb 8:5; Acts 7:44; 1 Chr 28:19; Rev 4-5.

01:heavenizing.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:heavenizing.label: Remodelling earth after heaven
01:heavenizing.def: The Spirit begins and man continues the task of reshaping earth's raw material after the heavenly pattern, moving it "from glory to glory".

01:glory-cloud.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:glory-cloud.label: Glory-cloud (portable heaven)
01:glory-cloud.def: God's visible throne-environment in the world (light, cloud, fire, thunder, rainbow) that leads, shades and fills the sanctuary.
01:glory-cloud.christ: In Rev 10:1 the exalted Christ comes “…”, the rainbow on His head (ch. 6, pp. 76-77).

01:hovering-spirit.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:hovering-spirit.label: Spirit hovering over the waters
01:hovering-spirit.def: The Spirit coming from heaven over the deep, bringing heaven's pattern and the first light, so beginning the glorification of creation.
01:hovering-spirit.christ: The dove that stands for the Spirit hovered over Jesus at His baptism (ch. 8, p. 100).

01:firmament.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:firmament.label: Firmament-heaven (the sky as a boundary shell)
01:firmament.def: The blue sky made on day two: a visible shell between the waters above and below that symbolizes and dimly shows the highest heaven.

01:heavenly-sea.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:heavenly-sea.label: Waters above / heavenly sea
01:heavenly-sea.def: The upper waters above the firmament: the heavenly sea before God's throne, seen as the sky's blue and as a sapphire pavement.

01:earth-footstool.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:earth-footstool.label: Earth
01:earth-footstool.def: The lower environment, God's footstool, given to man as raw material to be shaped into a house for God.

01:initial-darkness.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:initial-darkness.label: Primordial darkness over the deep
01:initial-darkness.def: The starting state of creation (darkness over the deep, formless and empty), which is unfinished but not evil, and is the setting for the Spirit's work.
01:initial-darkness.texts: Gen 1:2; Ps 139:13-16 (the womb as the same pattern, ch. 9, p. 106).

01:night-to-day.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:night-to-day.label: From evening to morning
01:night-to-day.def: The day moves from dark to light; in history the Old Covenant is night (ruled by the moon) and the New Covenant is day (the Sun's rising).
01:night-to-day.texts: Gen 1:5; Mal 4:1-2; Col 2:16-17; John 3:2; Rev 22:5; ch. 5 n. 1 lists Judg 5:31; 1 Thess 5:1-11; Gen 32:23-30; Exod 12:29; 2 Sam 23:4; Luke 1:78.
01:night-to-day.christ: Christ is the rising Sun of Righteousness. Nicodemus came to Jesus by night, which reflects that the Old Covenant was night (ch. 5, pp. 56-57).

01:land.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:land.label: Land (Israel's domain)
01:land.def: The dry land is Israel's sphere in Old Covenant imagery; God's people were farmers and herdsmen of the land.
01:land.texts: Gen 1:9-10; Rev 21:19-21 (stones of the land vs. pearls of the sea).

01:sea.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:sea.label: Sea / waters below (the Gentile world)
01:sea.def: The sea is generally the Gentile world; sea monsters are Gentile powers, and the New Covenant mission moves out onto it.
01:sea.texts: Dan 7; Ezek 27:25-36; Jonah; Luke 21:25; Rev 21:21; Ps 148:7.
01:sea.christ: Jesus fed crowds with fish and chose fishermen as apostles, marking the shift “…” (ch. 8, p. 100).

01:eden-and-havilah.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:eden-and-havilah.label: Eden (foodland) and Havilah (land of raw materials)
01:eden-and-havilah.def: Eden is the central foodland and sanctuary; lands downstream such as Havilah supply gold and gems, which are traded back to adorn the sanctuary.

01:holy-ground.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:holy-ground.label: Holy ground
01:holy-ground.def: Sanctuary ground where the curse is removed, so feet must be bare; burning bush, Sinai, Tabernacle and Temple precincts.
01:holy-ground.christ: Christ has cleansed the world, so believers can now go barefoot in the dirt (ch. 8, p. 102).

01:cursed-ground.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:cursed-ground.label: Cursed ground (dust)
01:cursed-ground.def: Under the Old Covenant the ground is cursed; feet are shod and washed, and dust-dwellers are linked with the serpent.

01:holy-mountain.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:holy-mountain.label: Holy mountain
01:holy-mountain.def: The mountain of God with glory at its summit: a ladder from earth to heaven, copied in altars, pillars and the Temple site.
01:holy-mountain.christ: (Developed in later chapters.) Here Jordan notes the New Covenant moves from Zion to the Mount of Olives (ch. 7, p. 86).

01:gate-of-heaven.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:gate-of-heaven.label: Gate (foot of the ladder)
01:gate-of-heaven.def: The base of the ladder or holy mountain, where heaven meets earth and where judgment takes place: city gate, Tabernacle forecourt, base of a tree.

01:heavens-and-earth-polity.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:heavens-and-earth-polity.label: "Heavens and earth" as a body politic
01:heavens-and-earth-polity.def: In prophecy "heavens" can mean a nation's rulers or aristocracy and "earth" its common people, so cosmic language describes a society.

01:new-heavens-new-earth.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:new-heavens-new-earth.label: New heavens and new earth
01:new-heavens-new-earth.def: The end of an old order and the setting up of a new one: new rulers and a new people, not only a renewed physical cosmos.
01:new-heavens-new-earth.christ: After Jerusalem's fall God replaces the nations' lights with “…” (ch. 5, pp. 66-67).

01:heavenly-lights.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:heavenly-lights.label: Sun, moon and stars (general)
01:heavenly-lights.def: The lights of day four have six functions: lights (glory), signs, festival times, clocks, rulers of time, and the heavenly host.
01:heavenly-lights.christ: “…” (no longer lunar festival times, ch. 5, p. 54).

01:sun.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:sun.label: Sun
01:sun.def: The ruler of the day; it stands for God and the coming Messiah, for righteous people who shine, and for false sun-gods.
01:sun.christ: The Sun of Righteousness (Mal 4:2); John saw Christ's “…” (Rev 1:16); the sun-like bridegroom of Ps 19 points to the Messianic Judge (ch. 5, p. 56); “…” (ch. 4, p. 46).

01:moon.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:moon.label: Moon
01:moon.def: The ruler of night and of the Old Covenant festival calendar; it stands for the old order and the First Adam.
01:moon.christ: Moon and sun “…” (ch. 5, p. 57); Christ ends lunar festival rule (ch. 5, p. 54).

01:stars.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:stars.label: Stars
01:stars.def: Stars stand for rulers, angels and God's people as a heavenly host: Abraham's seed, church leaders, saints; and false teachers as "wandering stars".
01:stars.christ: The same right hand of Christ holds the stars and the man John, showing that the stars of Rev 1 are men (ch. 9, p. 105).

01:constellations.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:constellations.label: Constellations and zodiac (tentative)
01:constellations.def: Star groups that God apparently designed and named; possibly twelve portraits of humanity matching the twelve tribes, with four cherubic signs.
01:constellations.christ: Jordan suggests studying the tribes/signs as “…” but does not do it (ch. 5, p. 62).

01:astral-collapse.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:astral-collapse.label: Darkening and falling of the lights
01:astral-collapse.def: Sun darkened, moon dimmed or turned to blood, stars falling: a picture of a nation or empire's rulers falling under God's judgment.
01:astral-collapse.christ: Fallen national lights are replaced by the Sun of Righteousness, who heals (ch. 5, pp. 66-67). Those who trust the Lamb escape, as Isaac did through the substitute ram (ch. 5, p. 65).

01:day-of-the-lord.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:day-of-the-lord.label: Day of the LORD
01:day-of-the-lord.def: God's sun rises in judgment, exposing and burning sin; for the apostate this "day" becomes darkness and cloud.
01:day-of-the-lord.christ: Fulfilled at Pentecost and in A.D. 70; those who receive Christ's blood escape, and those who refuse become the sacrifice (ch. 5, pp. 64-65).

01:rainbow.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:rainbow.label: Rainbow (God's warbow)
01:rainbow.def: The covenant warbow in the cloud that always surrounds God's throne; a sign of the Noahic peace, echoed in the gemstones.
01:rainbow.christ: In Rev 10:1 the rainbow is on Christ's head, so He sees the world through the Noahic covenant (ch. 6, pp. 76-77).

01:rock.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:rock.label: God the Rock
01:rock.def: God as an unchanging Rock: strength, fortress and hiding place, judgment, foundation, and shade. Idols are mere pebbles beside Him.
01:rock.christ: The cleft of the rock “…” (Exod 33:22) is often linked with Christ the Protector (ch. 6, p. 72).

01:smitten-rock.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:smitten-rock.label: Rock struck through the cloud
01:smitten-rock.def: The rod of judgment comes down on the rock where God's cloud sits; God takes the judgment, and living water flows to the people.
01:smitten-rock.texts: Exod 17:2-6; Num 20:8-9; Exod 24:12 (covenant written on stone).
01:smitten-rock.christ: (inferred) The judgment-taking God points toward Christ; Jordan does not cite 1 Cor 10:4 here.

01:judging-stone.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:judging-stone.label: The stone that crushes
01:judging-stone.def: The rock as judgment: a stone that falls and crushes, as in stoning and Daniel's stone cut without hands; falling onto it, by contrast, saves.
01:judging-stone.christ: Jesus is “…”; Christ's kingdom is the stone that shatters the world kingdoms (ch. 6, p. 72).

01:living-stones.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:living-stones.label: Foundation, cornerstone and living stones
01:living-stones.def: God or Christ is the bedrock foundation of His house; His people are small rocks built into a living temple.
01:living-stones.christ: Christ is the chief Cornerstone; Peter is a “…” (ch. 6, pp. 72-73).

01:gold.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:gold.label: Gold (and silver)
01:gold.def: Heavy, radiant metal that shows God's glory; gold overlay on wood marks God's host as glorified.

01:stones-of-fire.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:stones-of-fire.label: Gemstones ("stones of fire") and pearls
01:stones-of-fire.def: Precious stones hold fire and frozen rainbow; set in the breastpiece and city walls, they stand for God's people (land stones for Israel, pearls for Gentiles).
01:stones-of-fire.christ: Because the High Priest wore the stones on his heart, God's people are “…” (ch. 6, p. 78).

01:refining-furnace.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:refining-furnace.label: Fire that refines God's people
01:refining-furnace.def: God's fire tests His house: gold-like saints come through, while wood-and-straw people burn, so affliction purifies the people.
01:refining-furnace.texts: 1 Cor 3:10-13; Exod 3:2-7 (bush = Israel in the furnace of Egypt, ch. 7, p. 85).
01:refining-furnace.christ: Christ is the laid foundation that the fire tests (1 Cor 3:11, ch. 6, p. 77).

01:high-priest-covering-cherub.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:high-priest-covering-cherub.label: High Priest as covering cherub
01:high-priest-covering-cherub.def: The jewel-covered guardian of God's holy mountain (Jordan reads Ezekiel's "King of Tyre" as Israel's High Priest), whose failure leads the nations astray.
01:high-priest-covering-cherub.christ: (inferred from p. 78) Christ carries the gemstone-people on His heart as the true High Priest.

01:trees-as-men.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:trees-as-men.label: Trees as people
01:trees-as-men.def: Trees stand for people, since both come from the ground; the righteous are fruitful, well-watered trees, and sanctuary wood stands for the host.
01:trees-as-men.christ: Jesus as carpenter is “…” of His trees (ch. 7, p. 91).

01:thorns.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:thorns.label: Thorns and brambles
01:thorns.def: The cursed ground's ugly growth, standing for the unrighteous: Cain to Abel's tree, and Jotham's bramble-king.
01:thorns.christ: The bramble-men “…” on Christ with a crown of thorns (ch. 7, p. 81).

01:two-trees.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:two-trees.label: Tree of Life and Tree of Knowledge
01:two-trees.def: The two central trees of Eden, which act as sacramental symbols; Satan perverted them by saying there was no harm in eating from the wrong one.
01:two-trees.christ: Adam's dealing with the two trees “…” (ch. 7, p. 81).

01:tree-of-life.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:tree-of-life.label: Tree of Life
01:tree-of-life.def: The life-giving tree that pictures God and His Messiah, and also the wise righteous person who imitates Him.
01:tree-of-life.christ: Explicitly Christ (above); the Christmas tree points to “…” (ch. 7, p. 93).

01:tree-provision.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:tree-provision.label: Trees as food, medicine and beauty
01:tree-provision.def: Trees give fruit for food, leaves for healing, beauty for delight and shade for protection; this is the life of the blessed people.

01:bread-and-wine.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:bread-and-wine.label: Grain and fruit as bread and wine
01:bread-and-wine.def: The two food plants of day three, grain and fruit, processed into bread and wine: Melchizedek's gift, Joseph's two officials, the Eucharist.

01:shade.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:shade.label: Shade (canopy of protection)
01:shade.def: Protection from the scorching sun given by a tree canopy, a great rock or the glory-cloud; all three share the same shape and function.

01:sheltering-tree.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:sheltering-tree.label: Great tree with birds of the nations
01:sheltering-tree.def: A kingdom pictured as a great tree on a mountain that shelters the nations as birds; true (Israel's cedar, Christ's mustard) or proud (Nebuchadnezzar).
01:sheltering-tree.christ: Jesus moves the parable from cedar to mustard, announcing a humbler kind of kingdom (ch. 7, pp. 82, 92).

01:arboreal-theophany.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:arboreal-theophany.label: God appearing at a tree (burning bush)
01:arboreal-theophany.def: God shows His glory in or at trees and wood; the burning bush leads in a line through Sinai to the wooden Tabernacle and Temple.

01:lampstand.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:lampstand.label: Lampstand (institutionalized burning bush)
01:lampstand.def: A golden almond-tree lamp, burning with olive oil, standing for God's people and the anointed royal line; the reed-shaft is a person.
01:lampstand.christ: “…” and the Shoot of Jesse (ch. 7, pp. 86-87).

01:rod.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:rod.label: Rod / staff (the arm of God)
01:rod.def: Wood cut from a tree that carries God's power in judgment and deliverance: Moses' and Aaron's rods, and hyssop for cleansing.

01:tree-ladder.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:tree-ladder.label: Tree as ladder to heaven
01:tree-ladder.def: A tree as a vertical link between earth and heaven: roots/base as gate, trunk as ladder, leafy crown as the glory-canopy.

01:counterfeit-ladder.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:counterfeit-ladder.label: False ladder (Babel, proud tree, idol groves)
01:counterfeit-ladder.def: Man's self-made ascent to heaven (Babel, ziggurat, pyramid, Nebuchadnezzar's tree, worship under leafy trees), which God cuts down.

01:altar.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:altar.label: Altar and pillar stone
01:altar.def: A miniature holy mountain and ladder to heaven, often set beside a tree; its four horns are the four corners of the earth.

01:cross.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:cross.label: The cross (tree, altar, ladder)
01:cross.def: The tree on which Christ died, also the altar whose four ends match the four horns, and the true ladder to heaven.
01:cross.texts: none cited beyond the altar and ladder texts (Gen 28:12).
01:cross.christ: Christ's blood on head, hands and feet matches blood on the altar's four horns (ch. 7, p. 90).

01:gods-grove.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:gods-grove.label: God's planting / grove of people
01:gods-grove.def: God's people planted around Him as a grove (Eden, Israel in Canaan, the Tabernacle boards), shaped by the Divine Forester into His house.
01:gods-grove.christ: The carpenter Christ both plants and builds: “…” (ch. 7, p. 91).

01:kingdom-wood.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:kingdom-wood.label: Changing dominant tree in each era
01:kingdom-wood.def: Each covenant era has its main tree: Eden's two trees, gopher, oak, acacia, palm, cedar, olive/cedar/cypress, fig, myrtle, mustard/olive.
01:kingdom-wood.texts: Diagram 7.2; Exod 26:15-25; Judg 4:5; 1 Kgs 5-7; Zech 1:8-11; Esth 2:7; Neh 8:15; Matt 13:31-32.
01:kingdom-wood.christ: New Covenant = mustard and olive (Mount of Olives) (ch. 7, pp. 86, 92).

01:fig-tree.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:fig-tree.label: Fig tree (Israel)
01:fig-tree.def: A standard symbol for Israel as God's priestly nation; its unripe figs fall in judgment, and Nathanael under it meets the true Ladder.
01:fig-tree.christ: The fig tree is linked with “…” as the ladder (ch. 7, p. 87).

01:animals-as-men.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:animals-as-men.label: Animals as images of human life
01:animals-as-men.def: Animals mirror human life more closely than any other creature; they share sabbath, covenant blessing and curse, and the death penalty.
01:animals-as-men.christ: Christ is called “…” and “…” (ch. 2, p. 23, quoting Frame).

01:six-animal-categories.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:six-animal-categories.label: Six Genesis categories of animals
01:six-animal-categories.def: Genesis 1 sorts animals into six kinds (birds, great monsters, fish, wild beasts, creeping things, cattle); Lev 11 uses five of them.

01:birds.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:birds.label: Birds (spirits; also nations)
01:birds.def: Creatures of the sky, so symbols of spirits, clean or demonic; in tree parables they are the nations nesting in a kingdom.

01:dove.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:dove.label: Dove (Spirit, new creation)
01:dove.def: The clean bird that stands for God's Spirit over the waters; its flight over the receding Flood pictures a new creation.
01:dove.texts: Gen 1:2; Gen 8:8-12; Matt 3:16; Gen 8:9 (clean birds choose where they land).
01:dove.christ: The dove hovered over our Lord at His baptism (ch. 8, p. 100).

01:great-monsters.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:great-monsters.label: Great monsters (Leviathan, Rahab, Behemoth)
01:great-monsters.def: The great sea/land monsters of Genesis 1, used for nations in revolt against God, as in the beasts of Daniel and Revelation.
01:great-monsters.christ: The Son of Man subdues the four sea-beasts of Dan 7 (ch. 8, p. 96).

01:fish.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:fish.label: Fish (Gentiles)
01:fish.def: Creatures of the "waters under the earth", the Gentile sphere; the fishermen apostles mark the New Covenant turn to the nations.
01:fish.texts: Gen 1:20-21; Lev 11:9-12; Jonah; Ezek 27:25-36 (apostles as fishermen and the feeding with fish are cited without references).
01:fish.christ: Jesus fed crowds with fish (ch. 8, p. 100).

01:domestic-animals.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:domestic-animals.label: Cattle / domestic animals (Israel)
01:domestic-animals.def: Animals living with and depending on man, his closest helpers; they come to stand for Israel, God's household people.
01:domestic-animals.texts: Gen 1:24-25; 2:18-20; Exod 20:10; Exod 21:28-29; 1 Kgs 7:25 (twelve bronze bulls = Israel).

01:wild-animals.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:wild-animals.label: Beasts of the field (Gentiles)
01:wild-animals.def: Animals living apart from man; they often stand for Gentiles, especially converted, noble Gentiles outside Israel.
01:wild-animals.christ: Jesus “…” in the wilderness as the dominion-taking Seed (ch. 8, p. 96).

01:creeping-things.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:creeping-things.label: Creeping things (dust-dwellers)
01:creeping-things.def: Animals of the dirt, linked after the curse with the serpent and evil men; swarming house-invaders are unclean.

01:serpent.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:serpent.label: The serpent (boundary-breaker)
01:serpent.def: Satan's agent and leader of the rebel animals; the pattern for all uncleanness as the dust-eating intruder bringing death into the garden.
01:serpent.christ: The Seed of the woman crushes its head (ch. 8, p. 96); note 14: the serpent can also symbolize God (Num 21:8; John 3:14).

01:beast.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:beast.label: "Beast" as a symbol
01:beast.def: A layered symbol: the garden beast, Adam in skins, Nebuchadnezzar made bestial, Daniel's beasts, rioting men; used for rebellious powers.
01:beast.texts: Rev 13; Gen 3 (garden beast; Adam in skins); Dan 4; Dan 7; 1 Cor 15:32; Acts 19.

01:dominion-over-beasts.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:dominion-over-beasts.label: Son of Man takes dominion over the beasts
01:dominion-over-beasts.def: Animals rebel under the serpent; the Seed of the woman, the Son of Man, crushes their head and rules the beast-nations.

01:clean-unclean.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:clean-unclean.label: Clean and unclean
01:clean-unclean.def: A symbolic line between animals (and so people), set by feet and contact: split hooves and cud, scales and fins, careful landing.
01:clean-unclean.christ: The distinction is removed in the New Covenant; “…” (ch. 8, p. 102).

01:sacrificial-animals.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:sacrificial-animals.label: The five sacrificial animals
01:sacrificial-animals.def: Ox, sheep, goat, dove and pigeon, the only animals that may be offered; they stand in for human beings.
01:sacrificial-animals.christ: Those who trust “…” escape as Isaac did by the ram; refusing “…”, Jerusalem became the sacrifice (ch. 5, pp. 64-65).

01:lion.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:lion.label: Lion (and the cherubic beasts)
01:lion.def: A noble beast picturing God's strength, Judah and Christ; ritually unclean only by Levitical criteria. It is a cherub face with ox, eagle and man.

01:angels.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:angels.label: Angels (cosmic stewards and models)
01:angels.def: Heaven's created host who run the world for God (weather, motion) and model praise, throne-bearing and guarding for mankind.
01:angels.texts: Ps 104:3-4; Heb 1:7; Job 38:4-7; Matt 22:30; Isa 6; Rev 4-5; Ezek 1.

01:heavenly-host.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:heavenly-host.label: Heavenly host (angelic and human array)
01:heavenly-host.def: The ordered company around God's throne: angels, stars and, as they mature, God's people, mustered as an army at age twenty.
01:heavenly-host.christ: The Church is the host that models the angelic one (ch. 9, p. 113).

01:cherubim.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:cherubim.label: Cherubim (throne-bearers and guardians)
01:cherubim.def: Four-faced angels who bear God's throne-chariot, sing His holiness and guard His sanctuary, killing those who defile it.

01:sanctuary-guardian.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:sanctuary-guardian.label: Guardian of the holy place
01:sanctuary-guardian.def: The office of guarding God's throne: Adam's job, passed to the cherubim after his failure, then to Levites, then to the Church.

01:maturation-to-glory.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:maturation-to-glory.label: Growth from formlessness to glory
01:maturation-to-glory.def: Creation's built-in programme: earth grows toward heaven-likeness and man from "formless" embryo toward angel-like glory.
01:maturation-to-glory.christ: Restored in the New Creation “…” (ch. 9, p. 107).

01:degradation.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:degradation.label: Downhill into wilderness and beast-likeness
01:degradation.def: After the fall the growth process runs backwards: the world sinks toward wilderness and man toward the likeness of beasts and creeping things.

01:image-of-god.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:image-of-god.label: Man, the image and symbol-maker
01:image-of-god.def: Man is God's special symbol and viceroy, the only symbol that also makes symbols, and he rules creation by naming and dominion.

01:three-special-symbols.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:three-special-symbols.label: God's three special symbols
01:three-special-symbols.def: God's own appointed symbols, beyond creation in general: Man, Word and Sacrament, which Satan perverted and grace restores.
01:three-special-symbols.texts: Deut 19:15; Gen 3 (word twisted, trees perverted, man corrupted).

01:word-of-god.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:word-of-god.label: The Word (heavenly blueprint)
01:word-of-god.def: Scripture as heaven's verbal blueprint: the sky is a scroll, and the "speech" of the heavens is found in the Law-Word.
01:word-of-god.texts: Ps 19; Isa 34:4; Rev 6:14; Deut 19:15 (OT/NT as two witnesses).

01:sacraments.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:sacraments.label: Sacraments (two non-verbal witnesses)
01:sacraments.def: Baptism and the Lord's Supper, God's non-verbal special symbols, forming a twofold witness; the Supper itself has two elements.
01:sacraments.texts: Deut 19:15; Gen 2:9 (the two trees as sacramental).

01:restored-persons.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:restored-persons.label: Restored humanity (two priesthoods)
01:restored-persons.def: Saved people redefined by grace as righteous: a double witness of the royal priesthood (believers) and the servant priesthood (elders).

01:human-symbols.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:human-symbols.label: Man's secondary symbols (words, memorials, dress)
01:human-symbols.def: Symbols made by man in three areas (language, non-verbal arrangements, clothing), each special (oaths, rites, uniforms) or general (daily life).

01:body-politic.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:body-politic.label: Body and body politic
01:body-politic.def: The parts of one human body match the members and offices of a society, because God is both One and Three.
01:body-politic.christ: The church is Christ's body (1 Cor 12; ch. 2, pp. 24-25).

01:first-and-last-adam.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:first-and-last-adam.label: First and Last Adam (governors of the eras)
01:first-and-last-adam.def: The two heads of the Old and New Creations, who are the true rulers of the night-age and the day-age, pictured by moon and sun.
01:first-and-last-adam.christ: Christ is the Last Adam (Rom 5:14; ch. 4, p. 50).

01:naming-before-making.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:naming-before-making.label: Symbol first, then reality
01:naming-before-making.def: God and man name or define first and then make; God declares us righteous, and then remakes us.

01:typology-glory-to-glory.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:typology-glory-to-glory.label: Successive imprints of the heavenly pattern
01:typology-glory-to-glory.def: History as a series of copies of heaven, each more glorious: Tabernacle, Temple, Ezekiel's Temple, New Jerusalem; first Adam to Last Adam.
01:typology-glory-to-glory.christ: Heaven is pressed onto earth “…” (ch. 4, p. 51).

01:judgment-unto-salvation.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:judgment-unto-salvation.label: Judgment that saves
01:judgment-unto-salvation.def: The same act of judgment destroys some and saves others: the stone, the smitten rock, baptismal waters, the refining fire.
01:judgment-unto-salvation.christ: Those who trust the Lamb escape the judgment on Jerusalem (ch. 5, p. 65).

01:two-or-three-witnesses.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:two-or-three-witnesses.label: Two or three witnesses
01:two-or-three-witnesses.def: Truth is confirmed by two or three witnesses; God's symbols come in twos and threes (OT/NT, two sacraments, two priesthoods).

01:four.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:four.label: Four (corners, horns, cherubic faces)
01:four.def: Fourness ties together the four cherub faces, four central constellations, four camp-leader tribes, the four altar horns (earth's corners) and the cross.
01:four.texts: Ezek 1:10; Revelation (no verse given); Num 2; Gen 49:4, 9, 17; Deut 33:17; Dan 7 (four beasts).
01:four.christ: The four ends of the cross bear Christ's blood like the four horns (ch. 7, p. 90).

01:twelve.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:twelve.label: Twelve (tribes, stones, apostles)
01:twelve.def: Twelve marks the full people of God: tribes, breastpiece stones, foundation stones/apostles, pearl gates, Elim's springs, and possibly the zodiac.
01:twelve.christ: (inferred) The apostles' names on the foundations (Rev 21:14) carry the twelve into the church.

01:seventy.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:seventy.label: Seventy (the nations)
01:seventy.def: Seventy stands for the nations of the world (Gen 10), whom Israel, the twelve, is to water and feed.

01:creation-week-pattern.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:creation-week-pattern.label: Three-, six- and seven-day patterns
01:creation-week-pattern.def: The creation week is a real time-sequence set as a pattern for man; later three-, six- and seven-day patterns always run from beginning to end.

01:astral-periods.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:astral-periods.label: Astronomical numbers (Barnouin, tentative)
01:astral-periods.def: Patriarchs' lifespans and Numbers census totals possibly encode astral periods (Enoch 365, Kenan 910, Lamech 777), marking Israel as a heavenly host.

01:six-six-six.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:six-six-six.def: The beast's number, which recalls the size of Nebuchadnezzar's idol and Solomon's 666 talents at his fall into sin.

01:twenty.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 1-9
01:twenty.label: Twenty (age of maturity for the host)
01:twenty.def: Enlisting in God's army at twenty marks a reached stage of maturity on the path toward the angelic "host" likeness.

02:five-fold-divine-work.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:five-fold-divine-work.label: God's five-fold work
02:five-fold-divine-work.def: God's way of building a world: take hold, restructure and name, distribute with commands, evaluate, rest.
02:five-fold-divine-work.christ: The Word is God's “…” who carries out the Father's plan. The glorified Son sits at the Father's right hand.

02:six-fold-rite.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:six-fold-rite.label: Man's six-fold rite of work
02:six-fold-rite.def: Man's version of the five-fold work, with thanksgiving inserted after taking hold: take, thank, restructure, distribute, evaluate, enjoy.

02:thanksgiving.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:thanksgiving.label: Thanksgiving (step 2)
02:thanksgiving.def: Offering creation back to God, in hand, before working on it. This step separates the faithful worker from the rebel.
02:thanksgiving.christ: Jesus gave thanks over the bread. “…” means thanksgiving (p. 128).

02:corrupted-rite.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:corrupted-rite.label: The corrupted rite (Cain pattern)
02:corrupted-rite.def: The six-fold rite without thanksgiving. It builds a city of man, debases the world, and ends in God's evaluating judgment.
02:corrupted-rite.christ: The restoration required Christ's whole work, His death and resurrection (p. 125).

02:eucharistic-rite.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:eucharistic-rite.label: The Lord's Supper as the restored rite
02:eucharistic-rite.def: Jesus' Supper puts the full six-fold action back at the centre of worship and re-patterns all human work.
02:eucharistic-rite.christ: Jesus takes, thanks, breaks, names (body and blood), distributes, and is tasted. Judas evaluates it as bad.

02:promise-then-command.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:promise-then-command.label: Gift before law
02:promise-then-command.def: God's word always gives the kingdom first and the rules for managing it second. Promise comes before command.

02:dividing-and-restructuring.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:dividing-and-restructuring.label: Covenant-cutting as dividing and restructuring
02:dividing-and-restructuring.def: To make a covenant is to cut something apart and rejoin it in a new form, which then gets a new name.
02:dividing-and-restructuring.christ: Eve, the Bride, is cut from Adam and restructured into one body with the New Adam. The Fathers read Adam's sleep as a type of Christ's death (note 3, p. 300).

02:covenant-renewal-cycle.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:covenant-renewal-cycle.label: Death-and-resurrection of a world
02:covenant-renewal-cycle.def: History's repeating shape: decline, announcement, exodus, establishment, history and decline, and judgment that is also a new announcement. It moves upward like a spiral.
02:covenant-renewal-cycle.texts: Gen 6–12; Exod; 1 Sam 4–2 Sam 7; Jer 4:23–28; Matt 23–24; Luke 9:31.

02:announcement.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:announcement.label: Announcement (stage 1)
02:announcement.def: God lays hold of a declining world. Through a prophet He announces judgment on the old heavens and earth and promises a new one.
02:announcement.christ: John's announcement was the preliminary judgment and Jesus' the full judgment (p. 259).

02:preliminary-judgment.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:preliminary-judgment.label: Preliminary judgment
02:preliminary-judgment.def: A partial, warning judgment with time to repent, given before the full judgment that ends a world.
02:preliminary-judgment.christ: John the Forerunner's preaching = preliminary judgment; Jesus' = full (p. 259).

02:exodus.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:exodus.label: Exodus (stage 2)
02:exodus.def: God moves His people from an old world to a new one through captivity, deliverance and spoils. It is the world-scale "restructuring" step.
02:exodus.christ: Jesus' “…” on the Cross fulfils every exodus (pp. 183–184, 259).

02:establishment.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:establishment.label: Establishment (stage 3)
02:establishment.def: God distributes the new world, gives laws, new names and polity, and sets up a symbolic world model as His sanctuary.
02:establishment.christ: New names (Father, Son, Spirit; Christians), the world as grant, new sacraments, and the New Jerusalem as symbol (p. 259).

02:history-and-decline.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:history-and-decline.label: History and decline (stage 4)
02:history-and-decline.def: The time after establishment when God evaluates faithfulness and applies sanctions. Before Christ it always slid toward judgment.

02:judgment-as-new-announcement.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:judgment-as-new-announcement.label: Judgment that announces a new world
02:judgment-as-new-announcement.def: The final judgment on one world is also the announcement of the next. It takes the place of the sabbath rest that sin made impossible.
02:judgment-as-new-announcement.christ: In Christ God can “…” a kingdom that cannot fail (p. 168).

02:serpent-assaults-bride.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:serpent-assaults-bride.label: The serpent seizes the bride in captivity
02:serpent-assaults-bride.def: An exodus step. While the people are outside the land, a serpent-figure (tyrant) takes or corrupts the woman to raise his own seed.
02:serpent-assaults-bride.christ: Demons ravaged Israel in Jesus' ministry, and the Jews assaulted Christ's bride in Acts.

02:holy-deception.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:holy-deception.label: Holy deception of the serpent
02:holy-deception.def: An exodus step in which the righteous trick the serpent-tyrant to protect the bride, turning the Eden deception back on him.

02:spoils.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:spoils.label: Spoils of the exodus
02:spoils.def: The wealth God's people carry out of captivity. It later furnishes God's house.
02:spoils.christ: Between A.D. 30 and 70 the Church spoiled the Old Covenant. She now “…” (p. 186).

02:victory-housebuilding.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:victory-housebuilding.label: Victory then housebuilding
02:victory-housebuilding.def: After the exodus and the enemy's defeat, God's people set up worship, build God's house from the spoils, and install priests.
02:victory-housebuilding.christ: After Jesus' exodus and priestly installation in heaven, “…” (p. 187).

02:sabbath-evaluation.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:sabbath-evaluation.label: Sabbath as evaluation and covenant renewal
02:sabbath-evaluation.def: The Lord's Day, when God comes to evaluate. It closes the old week and opens the new one, which makes worship covenant renewal.
02:sabbath-evaluation.christ: Weekly worship means leaving the old world behind and receiving the new kingdom for the coming week (p. 169).

02:spiral-history.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:spiral-history.label: Spiral time
02:spiral-history.def: Biblical time is linear and rhythmical. Patterns repeat with variation and increasing glory, so history moves in spirals, not circles.
02:spiral-history.texts: Gen 9:20–27 (Noah's judgment of Ham parallels the Fall but is "an advance in glory", p. 175).

02:maturation.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:maturation.label: From glory to glory
02:maturation.def: Each covenant replaces the previous one partly because the people have outgrown it, not only because they failed. Each world is more glorious.
02:maturation.christ: The Old Covenant was “…” compared with the New (p. 123).

02:world-land-sanctuary-order.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:world-land-sanctuary-order.label: Build order: world, land, sanctuary
02:world-land-sanctuary-order.def: God builds a world from the outside in: first the wider world (sea or nations), then a homeland, then a garden-sanctuary.
02:world-land-sanctuary-order.texts: Gen 1; 10; 12; Exod 25–40; 1 Kgs 6–8; Dan 4, 6; Ezra 1–5; Haggai 1–2.
02:world-land-sanctuary-order.christ: The same order in Christian culture: homes or catacombs, then a Christian homeland, then cathedrals (p. 155).

02:exclusion-sequence.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:exclusion-sequence.label: Exclusion from the inside out
02:exclusion-sequence.def: As sin matures, people are expelled from wider and wider zones: garden, then homeland, then the whole world.
02:exclusion-sequence.christ: In the New Covenant all believers have immediate access, with no symbolic restrictions (Heb 7–10; p. 155).

02:human-house-first.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:human-house-first.label: The living house before the physical house
02:human-house-first.def: God organizes His people into a social house (polity, law, dynasty) before He lets the architectural house that symbolizes it be built.
02:human-house-first.christ: Kline: the kingdom-people-house was God's true residence, “…” (p. 205).

02:world-model-transfer.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:world-model-transfer.label: The model imprints the world
02:world-model-transfer.def: A God-designed model (Ark, Sinai, cloud) is moved onto the new world, which is then formed after it.

02:pattern-from-the-mountain.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:pattern-from-the-mountain.label: Seeing the pattern on the mountain
02:pattern-from-the-mountain.def: Man climbs the holy mountain, sees the heavenly pattern, comes down, and builds or transforms the earth after it.
02:pattern-from-the-mountain.christ: Jesus went up a mountain to give the Sermon, “…” (pp. 117–118).

02:rending-and-resurrection.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:rending-and-resurrection.label: Tearing the house, raising it in glory
02:rending-and-resurrection.def: When God's house is torn apart, it is like a sacrifice being cut up (death). The more glorious house that follows is its resurrection body.
02:rending-and-resurrection.christ: In John, Jesus “…” before His death and is a “…” in His resurrection (Nereparampil; pp. 224–225).

02:worship-before-conquest.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:worship-before-conquest.label: Altar before conquest
02:worship-before-conquest.def: The kingdom takes a place first by worship and evangelism. Cultural and political change follows, and a city grows around the sanctuary.

02:law-wisdom-paradox.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:law-wisdom-paradox.label: Law, then wisdom, then paradox
02:law-wisdom-paradox.def: God's people move from written law (Moses) to wisdom (David, exile) to paradox (Christ) as they mature.
02:law-wisdom-paradox.texts: 1 Sam 10:25; Proverbs; Job; Ecclesiastes; Matt 5:27–42; 13:10–17; Heb 12:5–8.
02:law-wisdom-paradox.christ: Jesus' teaching and parables are the paradox stage.

02:fulfillment.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:fulfillment.label: Fulfilment as transformation
02:fulfillment.def: The new covenant does not abolish the old but brings it to an unseen fullness. The difference is one of glory, not kind.
02:fulfillment.christ: In Jesus' death the old Adamic covenant died. In His resurrection it rose as the New Covenant (p. 260).

02:typology.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:typology.label: Restoring type and symbol
02:typology.def: Each Old Covenant world foreshadows the New. Jesus and the apostles restored the symbolic reading that had collapsed into moralism (Pharisees) or allegory (Alexandria).
02:typology.christ: Jesus explained Old Testament typology on the road to Emmaus. John presents Him as the true tabernacle.

02:kingdom-growth.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:kingdom-growth.label: Gradual growth of the kingdom
02:kingdom-growth.def: After Christ, the kingdom grows gradually to fill the world, like a stone becoming a mountain, a deepening river, leaven or a mustard seed.

02:ladder-from-above.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:ladder-from-above.label: Descent from above
02:ladder-from-above.def: After the Fall, the true link to heaven must come down from God. Ladders built up from cursed ground are counterfeits.

02:man-agent-of-transformation.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:man-agent-of-transformation.label: Man, God's agent of glorification
02:man-agent-of-transformation.def: Man stands between heaven and earth at the top of the mountain and turns nature into culture after the heavenly pattern.

02:king.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:king.label: King (kingly or "basilic" office)
02:king.def: The ruler who first understands and names the world and then beautifies it. Kingship is exercised through service.
02:king.christ: “…” Christ is the True Davidic King.

02:priest.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:priest.label: Priest (priestly or "hieratic" office)
02:priest.def: The guardian who recognizes holy boundaries and keeps them, mainly by leading people in worship.
02:priest.christ: Adam should have led Eve to the Tree of Life “…” (p. 137).

02:prophet.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:prophet.label: Prophet (divine council member)
02:prophet.def: A member of God's council whom God consults. The prophet argues before God and announces the council's decisions to the people.
02:prophet.christ: In the New Covenant all believers become council members (“…”) through the Spirit and baptism (pp. 140–141).

02:seer.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:seer.label: Seer
02:seer.def: An earlier, less mature stage of prophet. He knows and proclaims God's will but is not consulted.

02:shepherd.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:shepherd.label: Shepherd
02:shepherd.def: A ruler trained by caring for animals. Serving the creation teaches him to serve and lead people.
02:shepherd.christ: Jesus learned leadership as a carpenter (p. 135). John 10 places the Good Shepherd in the “…” section (p. 268).

02:serpent.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:serpent.label: Serpent / dragon
02:serpent.def: A beautiful and wise beast that Satan uses to test the guardian. In exodus stories it is any tyrant who seizes the bride.
02:serpent.christ: Christ defeated Satan. When a man took the heavenly throne, Satan was cast out of heaven (p. 270).

02:bride.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:bride.label: Bride / Eve
02:bride.def: The woman placed in the Garden to be guarded. The serpent assaults her in the exodus, and she is found at wells.
02:bride.christ: The Church is the new Eve. Mary Magdalene symbolizes her (p. 269). Jesus is the “…” at the well (p. 190).

02:cherubim.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:cherubim.label: Cherubim guardians
02:cherubim.def: Angelic guards who replaced fallen man at the Garden gate and around God's throne. Their flaming sword marks exclusion.
02:cherubim.christ: The two angels at Jesus' tomb mirror the cherubim on the mercy seat (p. 269). The sword is handed back as keys (p. 264).

02:high-priest.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:high-priest.label: High Priest
02:high-priest.def: The single man allowed into the Most Holy once a year. He is the supreme Adam in the Garden-sanctuary.
02:high-priest.christ: Christ is the “…”. The resurrection fulfils the High Priest coming back alive from the Most Holy (p. 268).

02:priest-king.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:priest-king.label: Priest-king (Noahic polity)
02:priest-king.def: The ruler of a post-Flood city-state who holds sacred and judicial authority together over one of the separated nations.

02:world-emperor.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:world-emperor.label: World emperor
02:world-emperor.def: The imperial ruler of the exile era who gathers the nations under one throne and protects or punishes God's people.
02:world-emperor.christ: Christ is the True World Emperor before whom every local prince must bow (pp. 182, 279).

02:mighty-men.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:mighty-men.label: Mighty men / Nephilim
02:mighty-men.def: Violent rulers who build a single world state. They were the "heavens" of the pre-Flood world, and Nimrod tried to bring them back at Babel.

02:city-builder.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:city-builder.label: City-builder (Cain / Nimrod)
02:city-builder.def: The rebel who takes creation without thanks and builds a city of man as a counterfeit sanctuary.

02:tyrant.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:tyrant.label: Tyrant / captor
02:tyrant.def: The foreign lord of an exodus story. He enslaves God's people, seizes the bride, is plagued, blames the righteous, and loses gods and spoils.
02:tyrant.christ: Herod and Pilate shifted the blame. Christ's cross destroyed Satan while apostate Israel was plagued (p. 185).

02:converted-ruler.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:converted-ruler.label: Converted Gentile ruler
02:converted-ruler.def: A pagan lord who is warned by a vision or converted, then favours God's people and sets them over his realm.
02:converted-ruler.christ: Paul aims at Caesar's household (p. 250). Pilate's wife's vision fits the exodus pattern (p. 185).

02:new-adam.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:new-adam.label: New Adam
02:new-adam.def: The head of a new world who repeats Adam's place with more glory and office. Examples: Noah, the king, the High Priest, Ezekiel.
02:new-adam.christ: At the tomb Mary rightly took Jesus for “…” (p. 269).

02:younger-son.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:younger-son.label: Younger son who supplants
02:younger-son.def: The younger brother who replaces the older heir. The older is a type of Adam, the younger a type of the Second Adam.

02:barren-womb-son.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:barren-womb-son.label: Son from a barren womb
02:barren-womb-son.def: A son given miraculously at a turning point. He restores the nation, and his birth is equivalent to building God's house.

02:witness.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:witness.label: Faithful witness at court
02:witness.def: A servant of the pagan empire who serves it well while openly bearing witness to God. He does not compromise and does not rebel.
02:witness.christ: Witness-bearing “…”. Paul yearns to reach Caesar's household (p. 250).

02:remnant.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:remnant.label: Remnant
02:remnant.def: The faithful minority who keep worship going in a time of apostasy.
02:remnant.texts: 2 Kgs 4:23; 1 Kgs 19:18 (inferred); note 18 (p. 312) on the Elisha "Remnant Church".

02:nation-of-priests.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:nation-of-priests.label: Nation of priests
02:nation-of-priests.def: God's people set among the nations as a priesthood to evangelize, guide and bless them. Converts are their "children".
02:nation-of-priests.christ: In Christ the Jew–Gentile distinction is erased (Eph 2:11–22; p. 271).

02:noahic-gentile.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:noahic-gentile.label: Noahic Gentile / God-fearer
02:noahic-gentile.def: A converted Gentile who stays under the Noahic covenant, worships the Most High, blesses Israel, and lives outside the holy land.

02:gathered-enemy.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:gathered-enemy.label: Gathered nations against the holy camp
02:gathered-enemy.def: The nations gathered, like the sea, to attack God's land or city. Their defeat makes room for God's house.

02:world-model.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:world-model.label: World model (symbolic polity)
02:world-model.def: A God-designed structure that pictures heaven and earth, God's house, the body politic and the righteous person all at once.

02:tabernacle.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:tabernacle.label: Tabernacle
02:tabernacle.def: The Mosaic portable house of God, read five ways: God's house, cosmos, holy mountain (Sinai), body politic of Israel, and righteous person.

02:temple.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:temple.label: Temple-Palace
02:temple.def: The Davidic permanent house, a palace for God beside the king's palace. It is a more glorious, transformed Tabernacle.
02:temple.texts: 1 Kgs 6–7; 1 Chr 28; 2 Chr 3–4; 2 Sam 7; Ezek 40–48; Ezra 3:12; Hag 2:3–9.
02:temple.christ: Jesus calls His body the temple He will raise (John 2:19–21; p. 265).

02:ark-of-noah.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:ark-of-noah.label: Noah's Ark
02:ark-of-noah.def: A three-deck wooden house floating on the waters. In the Flood it is the only land, a world model, and a type of the Church.
02:ark-of-noah.christ: A type of the Church, God's new creation (p. 172).

02:dove.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:dove.label: Dove over the waters
02:dove.def: The bird hovering over the receding waters at the re-creation. It recalls the Spirit at creation and at Jesus' baptism.

02:warbow.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:warbow.label: Rainbow / warbow
02:warbow.def: God's weapon hung up in the sky as the sign of the Noahic covenant. It marks a turn from wrath to grace.

02:flaming-sword.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:flaming-sword.label: Flaming sword / keys
02:flaming-sword.def: The cherubim's weapon barring the way back into the Garden. In the New Covenant it is handed to the apostles as the keys.
02:flaming-sword.christ: When heaven is opened, the keys (excommunication) pass to Peter and the apostles (p. 264).

02:robe-of-authority.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:robe-of-authority.label: Robe of authority
02:robe-of-authority.def: The garment of rule and judicial office. Adam was to grow into it, Noah received it, and Ham grabbed at it.
02:robe-of-authority.christ: — (p. 268 notes that the High Priest's garments of glory and beauty are put back on at the resurrection).

02:vineyard.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:vineyard.label: Noah's vineyard
02:vineyard.def: Noah's planting after the Flood. It parallels the Garden and is the scene of a new fall, but it is not a sanctuary.

02:tower-of-babel.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:tower-of-babel.label: Tower of Babel
02:tower-of-babel.def: A counterfeit holy mountain and ladder, built from cursed ground upward, to seize land, name and priestly mediation.
02:tower-of-babel.christ: Jacob's true “…” is fulfilled when the New Jerusalem descends at Pentecost (pp. 158, 191).

02:ladder-to-heaven.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:ladder-to-heaven.label: Ladder to heaven
02:ladder-to-heaven.def: Any structure linking earth to heaven: mountain, pyramid, altar, tree, pillar, sanctuary. Every heaven-and-earth model is also one.
02:ladder-to-heaven.christ: The Temple and Tabernacle symbolized the righteous person “…” (pp. 161–163).

02:altar.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:altar.label: Altar (mountain of God)
02:altar.def: A four-cornered earth platform that is a small holy mountain and world. Fire on it is judgment, falling on a substitute or on humanity.

02:pillar.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:pillar.label: Standing stone pillar
02:pillar.def: Jacob's anointed stone at Bethel. It is a "house of God" and a sign that the cloud will come down on the holy mountain.
02:pillar.christ: The descent of the oil or cloud is fulfilled in the Spirit's descent on Jesus at His baptism and on the Church at Pentecost (p. 192).

02:anointing-oil.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:anointing-oil.label: Oil poured from above
02:anointing-oil.def: Oil poured on a pillar, house or priest. It stands for God's cloud settling on the mountain, which is the Spirit.
02:anointing-oil.christ: The Spirit on Jesus at His baptism and on the Church at Pentecost (p. 192).

02:sacred-tree.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:sacred-tree.label: Sacred tree / grove
02:sacred-tree.def: A tree beside an altar or sanctuary, giving glory and shade. It is a ladder to heaven and a figure of people.
02:sacred-tree.christ: The mustard seed becomes the largest garden tree, sheltering the nations (p. 286).

02:tree-of-life.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:tree-of-life.label: Tree of Life
02:tree-of-life.def: The Garden tree of grace and life. It was the right place for priestly worship and the guardian's refuge from the serpent.

02:tree-of-knowledge.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:tree-of-knowledge.label: Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil
02:tree-of-knowledge.def: The withheld tree of rules and judicial maturity. In time it would have made Adam a ruler and a prophet.

02:well.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:well.label: Well / spring
02:well.def: Water dug up for the nations at patriarchal sanctuaries. It is the place where brides are found.
02:well.christ: Jesus presents Himself as the “…” at Jacob's well (p. 190).

02:stars-and-dust.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:stars-and-dust.label: Stars and dust
02:stars-and-dust.def: The double promise that Abraham's seed will fill the earth like dust and rule it like stars, a new heaven and earth made of people.
02:stars-and-dust.christ: The saints seated with Christ “…” (Phil 2:15). Church elders are the seven stars (p. 270).

02:river.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:river.label: River out of the sanctuary
02:river.def: Water flowing from God's dwelling to the world. It grows from cut-off river, to wells, laver, sea, one-way river, and finally the four-fold heavenly river.

02:laver.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:laver.label: Laver of cleansing
02:laver.def: The courtyard washbasin by the altar. It stands for the waters (Eden's, or the heavenly sea) and cleansing, above ground but not flowing out.
02:laver.christ: John 1–5 is the “…” section: baptism, purification, new birth, Bethesda (p. 267).

02:bronze-sea.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:bronze-sea.label: Bronze sea
02:bronze-sea.def: Solomon's huge basin on twelve bulls, which replaced the laver. It is a three-zone model with Israel encamped beneath it.

02:lampstand.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:lampstand.label: Lampstand
02:lampstand.def: A tree of lights in the Holy Place. It stands for the stars, the rulers as lights, and the Spirit's seven-fold presence.
02:lampstand.christ: John 8–12 is the “…” section, with Jesus as light of the world. Each church is now its own lampstand (note 12, p. 312).

02:showbread.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:showbread.label: Table of showbread / manna
02:showbread.def: Bread before God's face in the Holy Place, standing for manna from heaven. Eating it makes the people a heavenly people.

02:incense.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:incense.label: Incense
02:incense.def: Sweet smoke from the golden altar. It stands for prayer and copies the glory-cloud in the firmament-heavens.

02:ark-of-the-covenant.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:ark-of-the-covenant.label: Ark of the Covenant and mercy seat
02:ark-of-the-covenant.def: God's footstool beneath His cherubim throne, holding law, manna and rod. It stands for the earth or humanity under God and for the heart.
02:ark-of-the-covenant.christ: The two angels at head and foot of Jesus' burial place mirror the mercy seat's cherubim (p. 269).

02:veils.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:veils.label: Veils and coverings
02:veils.def: Layered curtains standing for ranks of guardians (angels, priests, Levites, Israel, Gentiles). They are "shoes" between God and cursed humanity.
02:veils.christ: Before “…”, access to the council was partial (p. 140).

02:glory-cloud.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:glory-cloud.label: Glory-cloud (Spirit)
02:glory-cloud.def: God's visible presence on the mountain and in the house. It is light, sound, smoke and manna, and it is the Spirit.
02:glory-cloud.christ: At Pentecost the cloud filled the house, and the New Jerusalem “…” (p. 274). John 1:14 “…”.

02:jachin-and-boaz.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:jachin-and-boaz.label: Bronze pillars Jachin and Boaz
02:jachin-and-boaz.def: Two Temple pillars standing for High Priest and King as guardians. Each pillar is a three-tier ladder: shaft, collar, lily.

02:chariot.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:chariot.label: God's chariot (cherubic and water chariots)
02:chariot.def: God's mobile throne: four cherubim and ten water-stands in the Temple. It leaves in Ezekiel; in Zechariah chariots ride out to cleanse.

02:bread-broken.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:bread-broken.label: Bread broken into a body
02:bread-broken.def: Bread taken, thanked over, broken and renamed as Christ's body. It is the paradigm for people restructured into the Church.
02:bread-broken.christ: The bread becomes His body. People broken by the Word are restructured into the body of Christ (p. 127).

02:tithe.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:tithe.label: Tithe
02:tithe.def: The tenth of man's work given to God on the sabbath. It is evaluated as the part standing for the whole.

02:passover.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:passover.label: Passover
02:passover.def: The centre of Mosaic sacramental law. It claims the firstborn and the blood-marked houses, and the whole Tabernacle system grows from it.

02:new-jerusalem.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:new-jerusalem.label: New Jerusalem
02:new-jerusalem.def: A gem-covered hollow pyramid that comes down from heaven over the highest mountain. It is Church, sanctuary and land in one.
02:new-jerusalem.christ: It is the Church, which “…”. Jordan reads it first of the Gospel age (pp. 269–274).

02:tribute-of-nations.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:tribute-of-nations.label: Gems and tribute of the nations
02:tribute-of-nations.def: Gold and gems from the outlying lands brought to adorn God's house. They show that the house is finished only when the nations come in.

02:leaven.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:leaven.label: Leaven
02:leaven.def: A symbol of growth, not of evil. Old leaven (Egypt, the Pharisees) is cut off and new kingdom leaven started in the land.
02:leaven.christ: The kingdom is like leaven working through the dough (Matt 13:33; p. 286).

02:covenant-garment.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:covenant-garment.label: Covenant as garment
02:covenant-garment.def: Each heavens-and-earth order is a garment. It wears thin or is outgrown and has to be replaced, not patched.

02:counterfeit-sanctuary.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:counterfeit-sanctuary.label: Counterfeit sanctuary
02:counterfeit-sanctuary.def: A sanctuary, priesthood or exodus made by humans in rebellion. It copies God's pattern without God's design.

02:three-decker-world.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:three-decker-world.label: Three-decker universe
02:three-decker-world.def: The vertical world: heaven above, land in the middle, sea or abyss below. Morally it is heaven, earth and hell.
02:three-decker-world.christ: A man ascended into the heavens, the Spirit changed the earth, and “…” (pp. 270–271).

02:highest-heaven.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:highest-heaven.label: Highest heaven
02:highest-heaven.def: God's throne-heaven, made on Day One. It is modelled by the Most Holy Place and was closed to man until Christ.

02:firmament-heaven.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:firmament-heaven.label: Firmament (sky-heaven)
02:firmament-heaven.def: The visible sky made on Day Two, an image of the highest heaven. Socially it stands for the rulers who are the "lights".

02:holy-land.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:holy-land.label: Land / homeland (Eden, Canaan)
02:holy-land.def: The middle, bounded homeland around the sanctuary. It is the earth deck laid out sideways and is given to God's priestly people.
02:holy-land.christ: In Christ the land–world and garden–land distinctions are broken down (p. 271).

02:sea.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:sea.label: Sea / abyss
02:sea.def: The lowest deck. It gives life, but after the Fall it images the Abyss and the restless Gentile nations that try to swallow the land.
02:sea.christ: Because the Gentiles are pictured as sea, in the New Jerusalem “…” (p. 271).

02:three-environments.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:three-environments.label: Garden, Eden, world
02:three-environments.def: The horizontal world: sanctuary (meet God), homeland (rest), outlying lands (work). It is the three-decker world laid out on the ground.

02:garden-sanctuary.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:garden-sanctuary.label: Garden-sanctuary
02:garden-sanctuary.def: The innermost earthly zone, where man meets God at appointed times. It is the contact point with heaven, guarded, and later the courtyard.
02:garden-sanctuary.christ: The garden outside Jesus' tomb recalls the garden-sanctuary (p. 269).

02:outlying-world.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:outlying-world.label: Outlying world (the nations)
02:outlying-world.def: The lands beyond the homeland, reached by the rivers. It is the place of work and trade, rich in gems, and pictured as the sea.
02:outlying-world.christ: In the New Testament “…” comes to mean the realm outside the Kingdom altogether (p. 271).

02:five-environments.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:five-environments.label: Five environments (Mosaic)
02:five-environments.def: The Mosaic scale of access: highest heaven, firmament, garden-sanctuary, holy land, world. Each has its own occupants and guardians.
02:five-environments.christ: In Christ all believers have the same access, so the five environments no longer apply (p. 271).

02:two-environments.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:two-environments.label: Inside and outside the City
02:two-environments.def: The New Covenant map: inside the New Jerusalem (heaven, sanctuary and land combined) and outside it (world and hell).

02:most-holy-place.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:most-holy-place.label: Most Holy Place
02:most-holy-place.def: The throne room behind the inner veil. It stands for the highest heaven, the cloud-capped summit, and the head or heart.

02:holy-place.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:holy-place.label: Holy Place
02:holy-place.def: The outer room with lamp, table and incense. It stands for the firmament, the elders' meal halfway up Sinai, the priests, and the senses.
02:holy-place.christ: Under the New Covenant all believers have access, where once only priests could enter (p. 270).

02:courtyard.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:courtyard.label: Courtyard
02:courtyard.def: The fenced area with altar and laver. It stands for the earthly garden-sanctuary, the mountain's base, civil leaders, and the outer life.
02:courtyard.christ: The Lamb is sacrificed outside, as on the courtyard altar, before His blood is presented in heaven (p. 268).

02:holy-mountain.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:holy-mountain.label: Holy mountain
02:holy-mountain.def: A height where heaven and earth meet. Man sees the pattern there and rivers flow from it. It pictures peoples and grows through history.
02:holy-mountain.christ: Jesus moved His kingdom to Olivet. The New Jerusalem sits on the highest mountain (pp. 156, 158).

02:north.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:north.label: North (God's throne)
02:north.def: The direction of God's throne and of Eden's source. Men live in the centre and the outlying world lies south.

02:gehenna.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:gehenna.label: Gehenna / the pit
02:gehenna.def: The ravine south of and below Zion, the base gutter of the altar-mountain. It is a symbol of hell or the Abyss.
02:gehenna.texts: Ezek 43:14, 17; 2 Kgs 23:10; Jer 7:31; 1 Kgs 18:32–38 (Elijah's trench); Matt 5:29–30.
02:gehenna.christ: Jesus uses “…” for everlasting punishment (note 15, p. 308).

02:captivity-land.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:captivity-land.label: Land of captivity (north or south)
02:captivity-land.def: The foreign land God's people are driven into, either north (Babylon, Mesopotamia) or south (Egypt, Philistia). Every exodus starts there.

02:oasis-sanctuary.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:oasis-sanctuary.label: Oasis-sanctuary / high place
02:oasis-sanctuary.def: An open-air grove of altar, tree and well set up by men under God's guidance. It is a "shadow garden" without a house.

02:synagogue.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:synagogue.label: Synagogue (local convocation)
02:synagogue.def: Local sabbath worship of word and prayer without sacrifice. It is pastored by Levites, then by prophet-trained laymen, and becomes the Church.
02:synagogue.christ: In the New Covenant the sacraments moved from the Temple to the synagogue “…” (p. 264).

02:four-corners.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:four-corners.label: Four corners
02:four-corners.def: The four-fold spreading of the Edenic pattern to the whole earth, through rivers, cherub faces, camp sides, altar horns and the cross.
02:four-corners.christ: The four limbs of the cross. Christ is the fourth and chief cornerstone with Peter, James and John (p. 148).

02:land-and-sea.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:land-and-sea.label: Land versus sea (Israel versus nations)
02:land-and-sea.def: After the Fall, the line between land and sea pictures the line between God's people and the restless ungodly nations.
02:land-and-sea.christ: In the New Jerusalem there is “…”, because the Jew–Gentile split is ended (p. 271).

02:rulers-as-heavens.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:rulers-as-heavens.label: Rulers as the heavens
02:rulers-as-heavens.def: Politically, the heavens are the rulers and the earth is the ruled. Every world has its own political heavens.
02:rulers-as-heavens.christ: Israel's heavens fell in A.D. 70. The Church and her elders are the new heavens (p. 270).

02:garden-to-city.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:garden-to-city.label: From Garden to City
02:garden-to-city.def: History runs from raw glory to worked glory, from Eden's garden to the New Jerusalem city, as man turns nature into culture.

02:two-adams.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:two-adams.label: Two Adams, two covenants
02:two-adams.def: Underneath every sub-covenant, history has two orders: the Old (in Adam, under curse) and the New (in Christ).
02:two-adams.christ: The whole Old Covenant “…”. Christ fulfils it and creates the new (pp. 259–260).

02:house-and-altar.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:house-and-altar.label: World as house and as altar
02:house-and-altar.def: Two complementary pictures of the world: a house that contains man, and an altar-platform on which man stands and offers himself.

02:three.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:three.label: Three (tiers or zones)
02:three.def: The standard division of a world model (three decks, three zones, three rooms or levels). Each tier matches a rank of people.

02:seven.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:seven.label: Seven (lamps, churches, eras)
02:seven.def: The number of the lamps and stars, and in Revelation the seven churches matching seven stages of Old Covenant history.
02:seven.christ: The risen Lord walks among the seven lampstands of the churches (Rev 2:1; Diagram 18.2).

02:twelve.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:twelve.label: Twelve (tribes)
02:twelve.def: Israel as an ordered body: twelve tribes, loaves, bulls and stones. Each set pictures the nation around God's presence.

02:seventy.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:seventy.label: Seventy (nations)
02:seventy.def: The symbolic count of the world's nations, set up by the scattering at Babel. It is the Noahic world's "symbol".

02:number-666.work: James B. Jordan, Through New Eyes (1988), chs. 10-19
02:number-666.label: 666 (Solomon's gold)
02:number-666.def: Solomon's yearly gold income, which marks his slide into tyranny against the laws of kingship.

03:image-of-god.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:image-of-god.label: Man as God's image and symbol-maker
03:image-of-god.def: Humanity as God's primary, special symbol: the one created symbol that also makes symbols.

03:dragon.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:dragon.label: Serpent-tempter who invades the sanctuary
03:dragon.def: The animal that invades the garden, attacks the bride and urges man to seize godhood now instead of waiting.
03:dragon.christ: Jordan's dragon speech echoes the temptation of Jesus (Matt 4:3,6) (RTD p.45).
where: RTD p.45, Jordan voicing the dragon

03:serpent-seed.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:serpent-seed.label: Offspring of the serpent
03:serpent-seed.def: People who carry on the serpent's line; born through the woman because she listened to the serpent.
03:serpent-seed.texts: Gen 3:15; John 8:44 (inferred; OCR lost the reference); Matt 23:33 (inferred)
03:serpent-seed.christ: The Pharisees are named as serpents, the serpent's offspring (RTD p.53 fn21).

03:woman-seed.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:woman-seed.label: Godly seed of the woman
03:woman-seed.def: The redeemed line that belongs to the woman, which Satan tries to kill.
03:woman-seed.christ: Not stated directly in these texts. (inferred: Christ as the seed)

03:bride.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:bride.label: Bride under attack
03:bride.def: The woman, or God's people, whom the serpent tries to take or defile in order to raise up his own seed.
03:bride.christ: The church is the Bride, and Word and sacrament show “…” (SM p.5). In a larger sense “…” (RTD p.66 fn47).

03:guardian-husband.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:guardian-husband.label: Husband who must guard the bride
03:guardian-husband.def: The covenant head charged with guarding the bride and the sanctuary against an invader.
03:guardian-husband.christ: The officers stand for the Heavenly Bridegroom before the Bride (SM p.5).

03:draconic-king.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:draconic-king.label: Tyrant ruler who thinks himself a god
03:draconic-king.def: A foreign ruler who seizes the bride, breaks the rules of hospitality and oppresses God's people.

03:satanic-accuser.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:satanic-accuser.label: Ruler or sinner who blames the righteous
03:satanic-accuser.def: The guilty party who, once exposed, turns and blames the righteous man (or God).

03:robe-seizer.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:robe-seizer.label: Usurper who grabs office before time
03:robe-seizer.def: One who takes judicial office or rule before God gives it, and so becomes a slave or beast.

03:patient-heir.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:patient-heir.label: One who waits for God's investiture
03:patient-heir.def: The faithful person who has the promise but waits, sometimes for generations, for God to give the robe.
03:patient-heir.christ: Christians wait as Christ was perfected through suffering (Heb 2:10; 12) (RTD p.62).

03:slave-who-rules.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:slave-who-rules.label: Faithful servant who gains mastery
03:slave-who-rules.def: A servant who, through humble and competent service under unjust masters, comes to rule in fact and later in name.
03:slave-who-rules.christ: Joseph's rule was partial and temporary; Christ's is complete and permanent (RTD p.67).

03:covering-sons.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:covering-sons.label: Sons who cover the father's shame
03:covering-sons.def: Sons who honor authority by covering its nakedness without looking, and are later given dominion.
