03:weak-deceiver.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:weak-deceiver.label: Powerless party who tricks the tyrant
03:weak-deceiver.def: A woman or subordinate, unable to fight directly, who deceives a serpent-like power to protect the bride or the seed.
03:weak-deceiver.texts: Gen 12; 20; 26; 27; Ex 1–2; Josh 2; Judg 4–5; 1 Sam 16:2; 21 (David feigns madness); 2 Sam 15–17

03:kinsman-redeemer.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:kinsman-redeemer.label: Next of kin who rescues or avenges
03:kinsman-redeemer.def: The closest relative who must rescue captive kin or avenge blood, acting from family duty and not to take power.
03:kinsman-redeemer.texts: Gen 14:14-16; Ex 21:16 (inferred; OCR lost the reference)
03:kinsman-redeemer.christ: The death of Christ cleansed all the land, so blood no longer defiles it in this sense; Rom 13 makes the magistrate the avenger (RTD p.56 fn26).

03:friend-of-god.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:friend-of-god.label: King's Friend / confidant
03:friend-of-god.def: The trusted advisor who comes into the ruler's counsel, gained by maturing through service.
03:friend-of-god.texts: Isa 41:8; Gen 18 (inferred); 2 Sam 15:37; Esth 8:2,15; Luke 14:10; John 15:15 (inferred)
03:friend-of-god.christ: In the New Covenant all Christians may become King's Friends after they have matured through service (RTD p.69 fn51).

03:prophet-mediator.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:prophet-mediator.label: Prophet as one who stands between
03:prophet-mediator.def: The one who speaks God's word into the world and speaks for two opposed sides, given to man after the Fall.

03:cherubic-guardian.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:cherubic-guardian.label: Angelic guards who replace Adam
03:cherubic-guardian.def: Guardians set at the garden after man fails to guard it, until human guardians are restored.
03:cherubic-guardian.christ: The Son of Man replaces them with New Covenant human guardians (RTD p.46).

03:beast-man.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:beast-man.label: Man made bestial
03:beast-man.def: A human who, by grasping at godhood or listening to the animal, becomes less than human and acts like a predator.

03:bird-of-prey.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:bird-of-prey.label: Oppressor of the covenant people
03:bird-of-prey.def: A tyrant power that comes down on God's people and on the covenant sacrifice, to be driven off.
03:bird-of-prey.texts: Gen 15:11,13; Jer 34:18-20 (inferred; OCR lost the reference)

03:tricked-one.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:tricked-one.label: One deceived into premature office
03:tricked-one.def: Someone tricked into taking office too soon; the blame rests mainly on the authority over them.

03:second-adam.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:second-adam.label: New head who receives the robe
03:second-adam.def: The man who, after the first Adam's failure, receives the robe of office on the basis of a substitute's blood.
03:second-adam.christ: Christ's resurrection and ascension are the guarantee that the saints will inherit and rule (RTD p.74). (Calling Christ the final “…” is inferred.)

03:robe-of-office.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:robe-of-office.label: Robe of judicial and royal office
03:robe-of-office.def: The garment that marks authority to judge and rule; given by God to the mature, never to be grabbed.
03:robe-of-office.christ: “…” because Christ is risen and ascended (RTD p.74).

03:nakedness.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:nakedness.label: Lacking the robe
03:nakedness.def: Man's first unrobed state, meant to be outgrown; after sin, the shame of holding office without wisdom.

03:animal-skins.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:animal-skins.label: Garments of skin
03:animal-skins.def: God's covering after the Fall: a sign of man's bestial state and a promise of office through a substitute's death.
03:animal-skins.christ: After Christ's death and resurrection the sign moves from sacrifices to bread and wine (RTD p.48 fn14).

03:robe-wing.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:robe-wing.label: Corner of the garment
03:robe-wing.def: The extended corner of the robe, standing for a man's dominion over the four corners of his life.

03:tree.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:tree.label: Tree as ladder of grace
03:tree.def: A sign of God's grace and of mature, righteous humanity, reaching from earth to heaven.
03:tree.texts: Gen 2:9; 28:10-22; Gen 18:1 (inferred, Abraham); Judg 4:5 (inferred, Deborah); John 1:48 (inferred, Nathanael)

03:thorn.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:thorn.label: Thorn as cursed tree
03:thorn.def: A tree in cursed form: it creeps on the ground, bears no fruit and shows God's wrath; also a type of the wicked man.

03:tree-of-life.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:tree-of-life.label: Tree of Life
03:tree-of-life.def: The foundation of life, offered at the start and not won at the end; man's source of life from God.
03:tree-of-life.christ: Christ is the Tree of Life; the sacraments are its continuing food (RTD p.42 fn7).

03:tree-of-judgment.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:tree-of-judgment.label: Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil
03:tree-of-judgment.def: The tree of investiture with judicial office; banned for a time, not forever.

03:wine.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:wine.label: Wine as sabbath rest
03:wine.def: The drink of rest after labor; it gladdens God and man and must be kept away from rulers while they judge.
03:wine.christ: In the New Covenant, wine is chiefly for the Lord's Supper, as Melchizedek gave Abram wine after battle (RTD p.49).

03:eating-flesh.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:eating-flesh.label: Eating animal flesh as investiture
03:eating-flesh.def: Permission after the Flood to eat meat, meaning the promised investiture is now taken into man's life.
03:eating-flesh.christ: The sign later returns to the vegetable realm (bread and wine) after Christ (RTD p.48 fn14).

03:divided-animals.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:divided-animals.label: Animals cut in half
03:divided-animals.def: Sacrificial animals split in two at a covenant-cutting, standing for man and land, with the curse of being torn and devoured.
03:divided-animals.christ: The covenant is restored only by a rending death, a substitute pointing to Christ, which leads to resurrection (RTD p.64 fn43, partly OCR reconstructed).

03:two-shoulders.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:two-shoulders.label: Shoulders as pillars and witnesses
03:two-shoulders.def: Two shoulders bearing something up stand for two pillars and so two witnesses.
03:two-shoulders.texts: Gen 9:23; Ex 28:9-12; 17:12; 1 Kgs 7:21 (inferred); Num 4; Gal 2:9; Rev 3:12
03:two-shoulders.christ: The incarnate Glory promises to make His people pillars in God's temple (Kline, quoted at RTD p.50 fn19).

03:opened-eyes.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:opened-eyes.label: Seeing as judging
03:opened-eyes.def: Eyes and seeing mean judicial evaluation; having "opened eyes" means having the office of judge.

03:stone.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:stone.label: Stone and precious stones
03:stone.def: Non-living things as symbols: God the Rock, and the Church as precious stones around God's throne.

03:star.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:star.label: Heavenly bodies
03:star.def: Sun, moon and stars as symbols of God's people and rulers; their collapse signals judgment.

03:animal.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:animal.label: Animals as images of man
03:animal.def: Animals are made from the ground like man, so they picture human life and can stand in for man in sacrifice.
03:animal.christ: None stated directly; the substitute points to Christ (RTD p.64 fn43).

03:glory-cloud.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:glory-cloud.label: God's garment of glory
03:glory-cloud.def: God's robe of light: His royal and priestly garment, seen as palace, temple and court.

03:garden-center.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:garden-center.label: Center of the garden as throne
03:garden-center.def: The garden's center, where the two trees stand: a picture of God's throne or footstool, the place of judgment.

03:ordered-earth.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:ordered-earth.label: The structured land (*erets*)
03:ordered-earth.def: The organized, structured world that God made; this is what the Flood de-creates and then re-establishes.

03:ground.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:ground.label: The dust (*adamah*)
03:ground.def: The dirt from which men and animals are made and to which they return; it is cursed, and it cries out over spilled blood.

03:formless-void.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:formless-void.label: Formless, empty darkness
03:formless-void.def: The state before creation, to which God returns the world in judgment before forming it again.
03:formless-void.christ: The darkness of Gen 15 is a sign of a coming “…” darkness (RTD p.64 fn40; the link to the crucifixion is inferred because the OCR is lost).

03:tent.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:tent.label: Father's private tent
03:tent.def: The authority's private dwelling, where he may rest and lay aside his robe; to invade it is to rebel.

03:pit-prison.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:pit-prison.label: Pit and prison
03:pit-prison.def: The low place of humiliation and suffering where the righteous gain wisdom and still rule.
03:pit-prison.christ: Joseph is resurrected from his humiliation (RTD p.66); a link to Christ is inferred.

03:city-of-refuge.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:city-of-refuge.label: Sanctuary for the bloodguilty
03:city-of-refuge.def: A God-given sanctuary where a killer may hide and be tried; God offered Himself as one to Cain.
03:city-of-refuge.christ: With the death of Christ all the land is cleansed (RTD p.56 fn26).

03:self-built-city.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:self-built-city.label: Cain's city
03:self-built-city.def: A city man builds to protect himself instead of hiding in God; the seat of violent, self-enrobed rule.

03:foreign-court.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:foreign-court.label: Land of a pagan lord
03:foreign-court.def: Foreign territory where famine or exile places the covenant family under a tyrant's power (the label is inferred).

03:grace-wrath.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:grace-wrath.label: Grace against wrath
03:grace-wrath.def: A pole running from blessing (tree, fruit, canopy, upward) to curse (thorn, barren, crawling, downward).

03:kingly-priestly.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:kingly-priestly.label: Serving and guarding
03:kingly-priestly.def: Two parts of man's task: kingly serving and filling (cultivation), and priestly guarding and separating (boundaries, judgment).

03:seize-bestow.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:seize-bestow.label: Grasping against receiving
03:seize-bestow.def: Whether office comes by grasping it early or by waiting for God to give it.
03:seize-bestow.christ: Jesus' parable of the wedding seats: whoever exalts himself is humbled (Luke 14) (RTD p.69).

03:youth-maturity.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:youth-maturity.label: Youth against maturity in wisdom
03:youth-maturity.def: Growth over time in wisdom gained through obedience; office belongs to the mature, and sin also "matures."
03:youth-maturity.christ: Jesus did not teach publicly until thirty (RTD p.69, partly garbled).

03:man-beast.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:man-beast.label: Man ruling or ruled by beasts
03:man-beast.def: Who rules whom: godly man over animals, or beasts (and beastlike men) over man.

03:older-younger.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:older-younger.label: Firstborn against younger
03:older-younger.def: Which son inherits; in Genesis the failing firstborn is often passed over for a younger son.
03:older-younger.christ: First Adam against second (OCR reconstructed, RTD p.62 fn36).

03:special-general.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:special-general.label: Special against general symbolism
03:special-general.def: Everything points to God in general; particular things or acts point in a special way to one Person or attribute.

03:verbal-nonverbal.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:verbal-nonverbal.label: Word against sign
03:verbal-nonverbal.def: How verbal a symbol is: from speech and texts to rites, objects, gestures and clothing; the two belong together.
03:verbal-nonverbal.christ: Preachers expound the Word, but “…” (SM p.8).

03:god-man-symbol.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:god-man-symbol.label: God's symbols against man's symbols
03:god-man-symbol.def: Whether a symbol is primary and from God, or secondary and made by man (righteous or sinful).

03:office-power.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:office-power.label: Office against power
03:office-power.def: Lawful office (to be obeyed within its sphere and under God's law) against bare force (yielded to only when actually used).

03:animal-vegetable.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:animal-vegetable.label: Animal realm against vegetable realm
03:animal-vegetable.def: The material of man's investiture: animal (skins, sacrifice, flesh) or vegetable (linen, bread, wine).
03:animal-vegetable.christ: The shift back to the vegetable realm comes after Christ's death and resurrection (RTD p.48 fn14).

03:covenant-creation-acts.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:covenant-creation-acts.label: Word, act, naming, witness, judgment
03:covenant-creation-acts.def: God's five-step creating pattern: command, separate or fill, name, see, judge "good."

03:sabbath-week.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:sabbath-week.label: Sabbath, work, judgment
03:sabbath-week.def: Man starts in God's rest, receives the word, works six days, then judges at the sabbath.

03:naming-before-dominion.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:naming-before-dominion.label: Name first, then rule
03:naming-before-dominion.def: Symbol comes before reality: God declares and it happens; man names his intention and then puts it into effect.
03:naming-before-dominion.christ: Justification (re-symbolizing as righteous) comes before sanctification (SM p.4).

03:lack-then-provision.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:lack-then-provision.label: God teaches by lack
03:lack-then-provision.def: God shows man an animal, man discovers a lack, and God fills it while man is passive.

03:seize-the-robe.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:seize-the-robe.label: Premature grasp of office (the Fall)
03:seize-the-robe.def: Tempted to skip waiting, man grabs judicial office, is exposed as unfit, judges wrongly, is cast out and clothed in skins.
03:seize-the-robe.christ: The dragon's speech echoes Matt 4:3,6 (RTD p.45).

03:cainite-maturation.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:cainite-maturation.label: Tyranny grows from youth to age
03:cainite-maturation.def: Abused office grows from murder to a city to boasted violence to mixing with the godly, until judgment.

03:de-creation-re-creation.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:de-creation-re-creation.label: Undo and remake the world
03:de-creation-re-creation.def: God returns a corrupt order to formlessness or darkness, then re-forms it and establishes His covenant.
03:de-creation-re-creation.christ: The Gen 15 darkness points to a coming “…” darkness (RTD p.64 fn40, partly garbled).

03:deep-sleep.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:deep-sleep.label: Deep sleep as death and new start
03:deep-sleep.def: A person falls into *tardemah*; a covenant is cut or something separated; death or resurrection follows.
03:deep-sleep.texts: Gen 2:21; 15:12; Judg 4:21; 1 Sam 26:12; Job 4:13; 33:15; Dan 8:18; Jonah 1:5 (several inferred)
03:deep-sleep.christ: The third-day/third-year resurrection theme (RTD p.63 fn39).

03:investiture-after-sacrifice.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:investiture-after-sacrifice.label: Robe given after sacrifice
03:investiture-after-sacrifice.def: After judgment and an accepted sacrifice, God renews covenant and gives man judicial office, sealed by a food sign.
03:investiture-after-sacrifice.christ: Investiture comes through the death of a Substitute (RTD p.48 fn14).

03:ham-invades-father.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:ham-invades-father.label: Son uncovers the father
03:ham-invades-father.def: While the father rests, a son looks at his nakedness, tries to recruit his brothers, the others cover him, and the curse and blessing follow.

03:attack-on-the-bride.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:attack-on-the-bride.label: Serpent-king takes the bride
03:attack-on-the-bride.def: A dragon-like ruler threatens the husband and takes the bride; the weak deceive, God strikes, the ruler accuses, the bride returns with spoil.

03:avoidance-under-tyranny.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:avoidance-under-tyranny.label: Yield, move on, be given room
03:avoidance-under-tyranny.def: Under a lawful but oppressive power, the righteous avoid conflict and move on; God blesses them and the oppressor seeks peace.

03:servitude-and-flight.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:servitude-and-flight.label: Welcome, enslavement, prosperity, escape
03:servitude-and-flight.def: A host turns oppressor; the servant works years, God sees and prospers him, he flees, and God restrains the pursuer.

03:wait-for-the-robe.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:wait-for-the-robe.label: Patient faith under promise
03:wait-for-the-robe.def: Holding the promise and the strength, the heir refuses to grab; asks for God's sign; covenant is cut; inheritance waits for generations.
03:wait-for-the-robe.christ: Believers wait as Christ, enthroned, waits until all things are under His feet (Heb 2:8) (RTD p.62).

03:earn-the-robe.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:earn-the-robe.label: From pit to throne through service
03:earn-the-robe.def: Stripped, thrown down and enslaved, the faithful servant rules from below, refuses illicit power, interprets God's word and is robed by the king.
03:earn-the-robe.christ: Joseph's authority was partial; Christ's is complete (RTD p.67).

03:younger-supplants-firstborn.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:younger-supplants-firstborn.label: Younger over older
03:younger-supplants-firstborn.def: The firstborn forfeits by contempt or rebellion, and the blessing or rule passes to a younger son.
03:younger-supplants-firstborn.christ: It signifies the failure of the first Adam and the faithfulness of a second (OCR reconstructed, RTD p.62 fn36).

03:wisdom-rise-and-fall.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:wisdom-rise-and-fall.label: Wisdom grows, then declines
03:wisdom-rise-and-fall.def: After the law is given, wisdom grows over centuries to a wise king's wide dominion, then he falls and decline follows.

03:forty.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:forty.label: Probationary forty
03:forty.def: The standard period of testing or waiting before investiture: 40 days, 40 years, 400 years, or 1657 years read as 40.

03:two-witnesses.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:two-witnesses.label: Two or three witnesses
03:two-witnesses.def: Pairing or tripling confirms testimony: parallel lines, doubled verbs, oath plus word, two shoulders, two Testaments, two sacraments.
03:two-witnesses.christ: The sacraments' two-fold witness shows Christ the Bridegroom (SM p.5).

03:three-third-day.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:three-third-day.label: Third day / third year
03:three-third-day.def: The third day or year marks de-creation followed by a new start before final judgment.
03:three-third-day.christ: The resurrection of Jesus Christ in the middle of history makes ours possible at the end (RTD p.63 fn39).

03:seven.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:seven.label: Seventh / sabbath
03:seven.def: The day of rest and judgment; also a marker of how far a line has developed (Lamech, the seventh from Adam).

03:six.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:six.label: Six years of slave service
03:six.def: The length of bond-service under the law, used to frame Jacob's labor as slavery.

03:thirty.work: James B. Jordan, Symbolism: A Manifesto (SM); Rebellion, Tyranny, and Dominion in the Book of Genesis (RTD)
03:thirty.label: Age of rule
03:thirty.def: The minimum age at which Scripture gives men rule or office.
03:thirty.texts: Gen 41:46; 2 Sam 5:4; Luke 3:23; Num 4 (inferred where the OCR lost the reference)
03:thirty.christ: Jesus did not ask men to follow Him as teacher until He was thirty (RTD p.69, partly garbled).

04:primordial-waters.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:primordial-waters.label: Waters of the beginning
04:primordial-waters.def: The first waters of creation: unformed, life-bearing, and the "seat" of the Spirit, from which heaven and earth were drawn.
04:primordial-waters.christ: The Fathers do not make the waters Christ. They are the Spirit's first seat, and every later water (Jordan, font) shares their "pristine privilege" once it is invoked over.
where: Tertullian, *Bapt.* 3 — “water is one of those things which, before all the furnishing of the world, were quiescent with God in a yet unshapen state.”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 3 — “Water was the first to produce that which had life, that it might be no wonder in baptism if waters know how to give life.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.5 — “the heavens are from the waters: the earth is the place of men, but the earth is from the waters”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.9 — “Consider, however, how ancient is the mystery prefigured even in the origin of the world itself.”

04:hovering-spirit.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:hovering-spirit.label: Spirit over the waters
04:hovering-spirit.def: The Spirit borne above the waters, who sanctifies whatever water He rests on.
04:hovering-spirit.christ: The same Spirit who hovered at creation "glided down on the Lord" at the Jordan (Tertullian, *Bapt.* 8).
where: Tertullian, *Bapt.* 4 — “the Spirit of God, who hovered over (the waters) from the beginning, would continue to linger over the waters of the baptized.”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 4 — “the Spirit immediately supervenes from the heavens, and rests over the waters, sanctifying them from Himself”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 8 — “Over the waters of baptism, recognising as it were His primeval seat, He reposes”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.5 — “before the whole six days' formation of the things that were made, the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the water.”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.9 — “He Who was moving upon the waters, was He not working upon the waters?”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 1.5.15 — “Water does not heal, unless the Spirit has descended and consecrated that water”

04:dove.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:dove.label: Dove (herald of peace; the Spirit)
04:dove.def: A bird sent out or coming down after the waters, bringing peace; read as the Holy Spirit and as simplicity.
04:dove.texts: Gen 8:8-12; Matt 3:16; Mark 1:10; John 1:32; Matt 10:16; Song 5:12.
04:dove.christ: The Spirit comes down on Christ at the Jordan, "the true Noe" (Cyril, *Cat.* 17.10). Through Him, the dove then comes on the baptized.
where: Tertullian, *Bapt.* 8 — “a dove was the herald which announced to the earth the assuagement of celestial wrath”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 8 — “after its old sins flies the dove of the Holy Spirit, bringing us the peace of God, sent out from the heavens”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 8 — “the dove is without literal gall”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.11 — “The dove is that in the form of which the Holy Spirit descended”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 4.24 — “that dove also which just Noah sent forth from the ark was a likeness of this dove”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 4.25 — “Rightly, then, did He descend like a dove, in order to admonish us that we ought to have the simplicity of the dove.”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 1.5.17 — “The Holy Spirit, however, descended from heaven, not in the reality of a dove, but in the likeness of a dove.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 17.10 — “the dove of Noe, according to some, was in part a figure”
Cyril, *Cat.* 17.9 — “He came down in the form of a dove, as some say, to exhibit a figure of that dove who is pure and innocent”
Augustine, *DDC* 2.16.24 — “perpetual peace is indicated by the olive branch which the dove brought with it when it returned to the ark”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.19.1 — “the coming of the serpent is conquered by the harmlessness of the dove”

04:raven.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:raven.label: Raven (sin that does not return)
04:raven.def: The first bird sent from the ark, which goes out and never comes back; it figures sin left behind.
04:raven.christ: Not related directly. It is the sin that baptism sends away for good.
where: Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.11 — “The raven is the figure of sin, which goes forth and does not return”

04:olive.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:olive.label: Olive branch, olive tree, oil
04:olive.def: The olive (branch, tree, oil) as the sign of peace and of sharing in Christ's "fatness".
04:olive.christ: Christ is the good olive tree (Cyril, *Myst.* 2.3). The exorcised oil means sharing in His fatness.
where: Tertullian, *Bapt.* 8 — “had returned with the olive-branch, a sign which even among the nations is the fore-token of peace”
Augustine, *DDC* 2.16.24 — “perpetual peace is indicated by the olive branch which the dove brought with it when it returned to the ark”
Cyril, *Myst.* 2.3 — “partakers of the good olive-tree, Jesus Christ.”
Cyril, *Myst.* 2.3 — “ye were cut off from the wild olive-tree, and grafted into the good one”
Cyril, *Cat.* 17.10 — “the dove returned to him towards evening with an olive branch”

04:waters-of-judgment.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:waters-of-judgment.label: Waters that drown
04:waters-of-judgment.def: Waters that destroy the wicked or the enemy while the righteous pass through or are carried over them.
04:waters-of-judgment.christ: Christ goes down into these waters (at the Jordan and in death) and breaks the dragon there (Cyril, *Cat.* 3.11). In Him the drowning waters become a grave that is also a mother.
where: Tertullian, *Bapt.* 8 — “the waters of the deluge, by which the old iniquity was purged”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 9 — “it was water that extinguished the king himself, with his entire forces.”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.11 — “All wickedness is there buried.”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 2.1.1 — “in that flood all corruption of the flesh perished, only the family and pattern of the righteous survived.”
Cyril, *Myst.* 1.2 — “was all at once overwhelmed and engulphed in the Red Sea.”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 12 — “disquieted "in the sea," that is, in the world, "by the waves," that is, by persecutions and temptations”

04:sea-monster.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:sea-monster.label: Dragon / whale in the waters
04:sea-monster.def: The beast in the waters (the dragon of Job, Jonah's whale) that swallows; read as the devil or death.
04:sea-monster.christ: Christ goes down into the Jordan to "break the heads of the dragon", and into death so that death "might cast up those whom he had devoured" (Cyril, *Cat.* 14.17).
where: Cyril, *Cat.* 3.11 — “According to Job, there was in the waters the dragon that draweth up Jordan into his mouth.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.11 — “The Life encountered him, that the mouth of Death might henceforth be stopped”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.12 — “suffereth thee not afterwards to be swallowed up by the terrible dragon.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 14.17 — “where the invisible whale of death is”
Irenaeus, *AH* 3.20.1 — “did God permit man to be swallowed up by the great whale, who was the author of transgression”

04:tyrant-in-the-waters.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:tyrant-in-the-waters.label: Pharaoh / the pursuing tyrant
04:tyrant-in-the-waters.def: An oppressor who pursues God's freed people to the water and is drowned there; read as the devil.
04:tyrant-in-the-waters.christ: Christ defeats the tyrant; the renunciation of Satan is said facing west (Cyril, *Myst.* 1.4).
where: Tertullian, *Bapt.* 9 — “the devil, their old tyrant, they leave quite behind, overwhelmed in the water.”
Cyril, *Myst.* 1.3 — “the tyrant was pursuing that ancient people even to the sea; and here the daring and shameless spirit, the author of evil”
Cyril, *Myst.* 1.3 — “The tyrant of old was drowned in the sea; and this present one disappears in the water of salvation.”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.12 — “wherein the Egyptian perished, the Hebrew escaped.”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.316 — “is choked with grief, and perishes, deeming the salvation of men to be his own misfortune.”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.298 — “Now let Laban be interpreted of the devil, and Jacob of Christ.”

04:deliverer-sent.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:deliverer-sent.label: Moses as the one sent
04:deliverer-sent.def: A leader sent by God into the land of bondage to bring an oppressed people out through water.
04:deliverer-sent.christ: Moses figures Christ, who is sent from the Father into the world (Cyril, *Myst.* 1.3).
where: Cyril, *Myst.* 1.3 — “There we have Moses sent from God to Egypt; here, Christ, sent forth from His Father into the world”
Cyril, *Myst.* 1.3 — “here, that Christ might rescue those who are oppressed in the world under sin”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 5.1.3 — “Moses, that is to say, a prophet; the rod, that is the word of God.”

04:egypt.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:egypt.label: Egypt (the house of bondage)
04:egypt.def: The land of bondage that the people leave through water; read spiritually as the world under sin.
04:egypt.christ: Christ is sent "into the world" as Moses was sent to Egypt (Cyril, *Myst.* 1.3).
where: Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.314 — “fleeing from Egypt, from the burden of sin, it is set free and saved”
Cyril, *Myst.* 1.2 — “God sent Moses to bring them out of the evil bondage of the Egyptians.”
Origen, *DP* 4.1.22 (Gk.) — “For if there be "spiritual" Israelites, it follows that there are also "spiritual" Egyptians and Babylonians.”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 9 — “The nations are set free from the world by means of water”

04:heavenly-jerusalem.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:heavenly-jerusalem.label: Jerusalem above
04:heavenly-jerusalem.def: The heavenly city that is the true subject of what is said about Jerusalem, Judea and Israel.
04:heavenly-jerusalem.christ: The Fathers do not tie it to Christ directly. It is the goal of the people Christ leads.
where: Origen, *DP* 4.1.22 (Gk.) — “it follows that the cities of Israel have for their metropolis the heavenly Jerusalem”
Origen, *DP* 4.1.22 (Gk.) — “we must understand the Scriptures as speaking of the heavenly city”
Augustine, *DDC* 3.34.47 — “such as Tyre or Babylon, are things said in Scripture whose significance oversteps the limits of the city”

04:exodus-through-water.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:exodus-through-water.label: Deliverance through the sea
04:exodus-through-water.def: People in bondage → sign of blood → pursued to the water → pass through → enemy drowned → freedom in the wilderness.
04:exodus-through-water.christ: Christ is the new Moses and the Lamb. The font is the sea where Satan "disappears" (Cyril, *Myst.* 1.3).
where: Cyril, *Myst.* 1.2 — “the door posts were anointed with the blood of a lamb, that the destroyer might flee from the houses”
Cyril, *Myst.* 1.3 — “Now turn from the old to the new, from the figure to the reality.”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 9 — “What figure more manifestly fulfilled in the sacrament of baptism?”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.12 — “holy baptism was prefigured in that passage of the Hebrews, wherein the Egyptian perished, the Hebrew escaped.”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 1.4.12 — “he who passes through this font, dies not, but rises again.”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 1.6.20 — “to them in a figure, but to us in reality.”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.311 — “The people passed over, and the Egyptian king with his host was engulfed, and by these actions this Sacrament was foretold.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.5 — “for Israel deliverance from Pharaoh was through the sea, and for the world deliverance from sins by the washing of water with the word”

04:paschal-lamb.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:paschal-lamb.label: The lamb and its blood
04:paschal-lamb.def: The lamb whose blood marks the doors so that the destroyer passes over.
where: Cyril, *Myst.* 1.3 — “there, the blood of a lamb was the spell against the destroyer; here, the blood of the Lamb without blemish Jesus Christ”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.19 — “I was like a harmless lamb led to be slaughtered”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 19 — “The Passover affords a more than usually solemn day for baptism”

04:pillar-and-cloud.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:pillar-and-cloud.label: Pillar of fire and cloud
04:pillar-and-cloud.def: The guiding pillar of light and the overshadowing cloud over the people in the sea.
04:pillar-and-cloud.christ: The pillar of light is Christ (Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 1.6.22). The cloud overshadows Mary at the Incarnation (Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.13).
where: Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 1.6.22 — “What is the pillar of light but Christ the Lord”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 1.6.22 — “The pillar of cloud, on the other hand, is the Holy Spirit.”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.13 — “That kindly cloud overshadows those whom the Holy Spirit visits. At last it came upon the Virgin Mary”

04:water-then-wilderness.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:water-then-wilderness.label: Crossing the water, then testing in the wilderness
04:water-then-wilderness.def: After passing through water comes a period of testing in the desert, numbered forty.
04:water-then-wilderness.christ: Christ repeats Israel's forty years as forty days and wins where Israel failed. Tertullian: "the Lord figuratively retorted upon Israel the reproach".
where: Tertullian, *Bapt.* 20 — “the people, after crossing the sea, and being carried about in the desert during forty years”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 20 — “the Lord, driven apart into desert places after baptism, showed, by maintaining a fast of forty days”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.13 — “For as after His Baptism He was tempted forty days”
Cyril, *Myst.* 3.4 — “as Christ after His Baptism, and the visitation of the Holy Ghost, went forth and vanquished the adversary”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 1.4.12 — “Yet the Jews who passed through all died in the wilderness.”

04:bitter-made-sweet.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:bitter-made-sweet.label: Marah: wood sweetens the water
04:bitter-made-sweet.def: Bitter, undrinkable water is made sweet when wood is cast into it.
04:bitter-made-sweet.christ: The wood is Christ or His cross. The sign of the cross over the font makes the water sweet (Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.14).
where: Tertullian, *Bapt.* 9 — “water is restored from its defect of "bitterness" to its native grace of "sweetness" by the tree of Moses. That tree was Christ”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.14 — “Marah was a fountain of most bitter water: Moses cast wood into it and it became sweet.”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.14 — “For water without the preaching of the Cross of the Lord is of no avail for future salvation”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.20 — “The wood in Moses' case sweetened the water; and from the side of Jesus the water flowed upon the wood.”
Augustine, *DDC* 1.2.2 — “the wood which we read Moses cast into the bitter waters to make them sweet”

04:smitten-rock.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:smitten-rock.label: The rock that gives water
04:smitten-rock.def: A rock struck in the desert that pours out water for a thirsty people.
04:smitten-rock.christ: The Rock is Christ. The water from it is baptism (Tertullian), the cup (Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 5.1.3) and His blood (Ambrose, *De Myst.* 8.49a).
where: Tertullian, *Bapt.* 9 — “if Christ is "the Rock," without doubt we see baptism blest by the water in Christ.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 10.7 — “For they all drank of a spiritual rock that followed them; and the rock was Christ”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 8.49a — “For them water flowed from the rock, for you Blood flowed from Christ”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 8.49b — “See now what happened in the case of the fathers was shadow”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 5.1.3 — “It was not an immovable Rock which followed the people. Drink thou also, that Christ may follow thee.”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 9.51 — “Moses touched the rock, and water flowed out of the rock.”
Irenaeus, *AH* 4.14.3 — “"For they drank of the rock which followed them: and the rock was Christ."”
Origen, *DP* 4.1.13 (Gk.) — “"For they drank of the spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ."”

04:pierced-side.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:pierced-side.label: Christ's opened side (water and blood)
04:pierced-side.def: The wound in Christ's side, from which water and blood flow: the two baptisms and the sacraments.
04:pierced-side.christ: The side is Christ's own. The Fathers make it the source of baptism (water) and martyrdom or the cup (blood).
where: Tertullian, *Bapt.* 9 — “when He is wounded, forth from His side bursts water; witness the soldier's lance!”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 16 — “These two baptisms He sent out from the wound in His pierced side”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.10 — “He shed forth blood and water; that men, living in times of peace, might be baptized in water”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.20 — “from the side of Jesus the water flowed upon the wood.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.21 — “Jesus at the last gave forth from His side water with blood.”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 5.1.4 — “Why from his side? Because whence the guilt, thence the grace; guilt through woman, grace through the Lord Jesus Christ.”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 4.20 — “the three witnesses in baptism, the water, the blood, and the Spirit, are one”
Irenaeus, *AH* 3.22.2 — “nor, when His side was pierced, would there have come forth blood and water.”

04:saving-wood.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:saving-wood.label: Wood that saves
04:saving-wood.def: Any wood God uses to save (ark, rod, Marah wood, serpent-pole, Elisha's stick); all point to the cross.
04:saving-wood.christ: All of these woods point to the cross. Tertullian also makes the wood Christ Himself.
where: Cyril, *Cat.* 13.20 — “On each occasion life comes by means of wood. For in the time of Noe the preservation of life was by an ark of wood.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.20 — “is then Moses' rod mighty, and is the Cross of the Saviour powerless?”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.11 — “The wood is that on which the Lord Jesus was fastened when He suffered for us.”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 2.4.11 — “Dost thou see, therefore, how the weakness of all men is raised on the cross of Christ?”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.17.4 — “which we had negligently lost by means of a tree ... we should receive anew by the dispensation of a tree”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.150 — “the wood of the Cross is of saving efficacy for all men”
Cyril, *Cat.* 17.10 — “He who by the wood of the Cross saves them who believe”

04:tree-of-knowledge.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:tree-of-knowledge.label: The tree of the fall
04:tree-of-knowledge.def: The tree in Paradise through which man disobeyed, lost the word of God and became a debtor.
04:tree-of-knowledge.christ: Christ undoes the tree of disobedience by His obedience on the tree of the cross (Irenaeus, *AH* 5.16.3; 5.19.1).
where: Irenaeus, *AH* 5.16.3 — “that disobedience of man which had taken place at the beginning by the occasion of a tree”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.17.3 — “as by means of a tree we were made debtors to God”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.17.4 — “For as we lost it by means of a tree, by means of a tree again was it made manifest to all”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.19 — “From the Tree came sin, and until the Tree sin lasted.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.31 — “Adam by the Tree fell away”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.20.2 — “For these men do profess that they have themselves the knowledge of good and evil”

04:cross.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:cross.label: The cross (the second tree)
04:cross.def: The tree on which Christ, the second Adam, obeys; it answers the tree of the fall point for point.
04:cross.christ: It is Christ's own cross. The outstretched hands gather two peoples under one head (Irenaeus, *AH* 5.17.4).
where: Irenaeus, *AH* 5.16.3 — “rectifying that disobedience which had occurred by reason of a tree, through that obedience which was [wrought out] upon the tree [of the cross].”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.17.3 — “[so also] by means of a tree we may obtain the remission of our debt.”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.17.4 — “there was one head in the middle, as there is but one God”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.17.4 — “two hands, because there were two peoples scattered to the ends of the earth”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.31 — “Adam by the Tree fell away; thou by the Tree art brought into Paradise.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.28 — “He stretched out His hands on the Cross, that He might embrace the ends of the world”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 2.7.23 — “Let the nail of Christ hold thee fast”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 8 (Jacob's crossed hands) — “by delineating Christ, they even portended the future benediction into Christ.”

04:bronze-serpent.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:bronze-serpent.label: Serpent lifted on a pole
04:bronze-serpent.def: The bronze serpent fixed on a pole; those who looked at it lived.
where: Cyril, *Cat.* 13.20 — “This was the figure which Moses completed by fixing the serpent to a cross”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.20 — “Does then the brazen serpent save when crucified, and shall not the Son of God incarnate save when crucified also?”

04:axe-head-raised.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:axe-head-raised.label: The iron raised by wood
04:axe-head-raised.def: Iron sinks in the water and is raised when wood is thrown in after it.
04:axe-head-raised.christ: The wood is the cross. In Irenaeus, the iron raised is the word of God that was lost.
where: Irenaeus, *AH* 5.17.4 — “he threw some wood into the water. Then, when he had done this, the iron part of the axe floated up”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.17.4 — “For that the word of God is likened to an axe, John the Baptist declares”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 2.4.11 — “every man before baptism is weighed down like iron, and sinks”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 2.4.11 — “Dost thou see, therefore, how the weakness of all men is raised on the cross of Christ?”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 9.51 — “This, too, we clearly recognize as having happened contrary to nature, for iron is of heavier nature than water.”

04:ark.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:ark.label: Ark / ship (vessel through the waters)
04:ark.def: A closed wooden vessel that carries the righteous through the drowning waters; read as the Church, and its wood as the cross.
04:ark.christ: The ark is the Church (Tertullian, Cyril), its wood is the cross (Ambrose), and Christ is "the true Noe" (Cyril, *Cat.* 17.10). In the boat Christ sleeps and then calms the world (Tertullian, *Bapt.* 12).
where: Tertullian, *Bapt.* 8 — “sent out from the heavens where is the Church, the typified ark.”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 12 — “that little ship did present a figure of the Church, in that she is disquieted "in the sea," that is, in the world”
Cyril, *Procat.* 14 — “For now I need the example of Noah's ark” ... “If the Church is shut, and you are all inside”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.20 — “in the time of Noe the preservation of life was by an ark of wood.”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.10 — “You see the water, you see the wood [of the ark], you see the dove”
Cyril, *Cat.* 17.10 — “of whom the various dispositions of the animals in the ark were a figure”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.304 — “laid in an ark, for it was fitting that the Law should typically be enclosed in a coffer”

04:righteous-remnant.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:righteous-remnant.label: The righteous one saved through the water
04:righteous-remnant.def: The one righteous man (with his household) kept alive through judgment to be the seed of a new world.
where: Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 2.1.1 — “What is the flood, but that in which the righteous is saved to be a seed-plot of righteousness, while sin dies?”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 2.1.1 — “he saved the righteous one alone with his offspring, but he bade the water rise even above the mountains.”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.10 — “God, willing to restore what was lacking, sent the flood and bade just Noah go up into the ark.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 17.10 — “the Holy Ghost also descended upon the true Noe, the Author of the second birth”

04:deluge-and-dove.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:deluge-and-dove.label: The flood shape
04:deluge-and-dove.def: Corruption → waters purge the world → righteous carried in a wooden vessel → bird sent out → dove returns with peace → a new generation.
04:deluge-and-dove.christ: Christ is the righteous Noah, the ark's wood is His cross, and the dove is the Spirit on Him at the Jordan. Tertullian warns that the world returned to sin after the flood, so the type does not fit in that respect.
where: Tertullian, *Bapt.* 8 — “after the waters of the deluge, by which the old iniquity was purged--after the baptism, so to say, of the world--a dove was the herald”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.10 — “You see the water, you see the wood [of the ark], you see the dove, and do you hesitate as to the mystery?”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 2.1.1 — “Is not the flood the same thing as baptism, whereby all sins are washed away, only the mind and grace of the righteous is revived”
Cyril, *Cat.* 17.10 — “by means of wood and of water there came salvation to themselves, and the beginning of a new generation”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.5 — “After the flood, a covenant was made with Noah”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 8 (the limit) — “the world returned unto sin; in which point baptism would ill be compared to the deluge.”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 1.6.23 — “if the figure of our baptism preceded, thou seest that the mysteries of the Christians are earlier than were those of the Jews.”

04:new-creation.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:new-creation.label: New beginning after the waters
04:new-creation.def: The end state after passing through water: a new generation, regeneration, a second birth.
04:new-creation.christ: The second creation comes "by means of His passion" (Irenaeus, *AH* 5.23.2).
where: Cyril, *Cat.* 17.10 — “the beginning of a new generation”
Cyril, *Cat.* 17.10 — “the true Noe, the Author of the second birth”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.83 — “Baptism, then, is a purification from sins, a remission of trespasses, a cause of renovation and regeneration.”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.23.2 — “thus granting him a second creation by means of His passion, which is that [creation] out of death.”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 5 — “Thus man will be restored for God to His "likeness," who in days bygone had been conformed to "the image" of God”

04:font.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:font.label: Baptismal font (grave and mother)
04:font.def: The water of baptism, which is at once a tomb to go down into and a womb to be born from.
04:font.christ: Going into the font is going into Christ's tomb (Cyril, *Myst.* 2.4).
where: Cyril, *Myst.* 2.4 — “that Water of salvation was at once your grave and your mother.”
Cyril, *Myst.* 2.4 — “ye were led to the holy pool of Divine Baptism, as Christ was carried from the Cross to the Sepulchre”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 2.6.19 — “the font is, as it were, a burial”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 4.23 — “that pool was as a type, that you might believe that the power of God descends upon this font.”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 1 — “we, little fishes, after the example of our IChThUS Jesus Christ, are born in water”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 20 — “spread your hands for the first time in the house of your mother”

04:burial-and-rising.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:burial-and-rising.label: Down into the water, up into life
04:burial-and-rising.def: Go down into water as into a grave (three times), come up as from the tomb, newborn.
04:burial-and-rising.christ: This is the participation in Christ's death, burial and resurrection, "in a likeness" (Cyril, *Myst.* 2.5–2.7).
where: Cyril, *Myst.* 2.4 — “descended three times into the water, and ascended again; here also hinting by a symbol at the three days burial of Christ.”
Cyril, *Myst.* 2.4 — “in the descent, as in the night, ye saw nothing, but in ascending again ye were as in the day.”
Cyril, *Myst.* 2.5 — “our imitation was in a figure, and our salvation in reality.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.12 — “Having gone down dead in sins, thou comest up quickened in righteousness.”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 4.21 — “you died to the world, and rose again to God.”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 2.6.19 — “a means was found that man might die while living, and while living rise again.”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 2.7.20 — “for he who is buried with Christ, rises again with Christ.”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.192 — “went beneath the fourth of these, the earth, that He might raise up life from thence.”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.197 — “coming to the element akin to earth, to water, we conceal ourselves in that as the Saviour did in the earth”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 2 — “a man is dipped in water, and amid the utterance of some few words, is sprinkled, and then rises again”

04:jordan.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:jordan.label: The Jordan
04:jordan.def: The river crossed into the land and used for washing and healing; where Christ was baptized; the source of all baptism.
04:jordan.christ: Christ sanctifies the Jordan by being baptized in it, and through it all waters (Cyril, *Cat.* 3.11; *Myst.* 3.1).
where: Cyril, *Cat.* 3.5 — “The water was the beginning of the world, and Jordan the beginning of the Gospel tidings”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.5 — “Elias is taken up, but not apart from water: for first he crosses the Jordan, then in a chariot mounts the heaven.”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.322 — “did not enter the land of promise until it had first been brought ... to the passage of the Jordan.”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.357 — “Jordan alone of rivers, receiving in itself the first-fruits of sanctification and benediction, conveyed in its channel to the whole world”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.400 — “the Jordan glorified by regenerating men and planting them in the Paradise of God”
Cyril, *Myst.* 3.1 — “He washed in the river Jordan, and having imparted of the fragrance of His Godhead to the waters, He came up from them”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 1.5.14 — “Then he went to Jordan, dipped, and arose whole.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 12.15 — “the sea saw Him and fled, and Jordan was turned back”

04:healing-pool.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:healing-pool.label: The troubled pool (Bethesda)
04:healing-pool.def: A pool where an angel from above stirs the water and the first to go down is healed.
04:healing-pool.christ: In *De Sacr.* the angel is Christ, "the Angel of Great Counsel". In *De Myst.* the paralytic waits for "the Lord Jesus, born of the Virgin" (4.24).
where: Tertullian, *Bapt.* 5 — “An angel, by his intervention, was wont to stir the pool at Bethsaida.”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 5 — “This figure of corporeal healing sang of a spiritual healing”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 4.22 — “They had a sign, you have faith; for them an angel descended, for you the Holy Spirit”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 4.23 — “that pool was as a type, that you might believe that the power of God descends upon this font.”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 2.2.3 — “Which signifies a figure of our Lord Jesus Christ who was to come.”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 2.2.4 — “Because he himself is the Angel of Great Counsel”

04:mediator-from-above.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:mediator-from-above.label: One who comes down on the waters from above
04:mediator-from-above.def: A heavenly agent (Spirit, dove, angel, voice, fire) who comes down onto water or a sacrifice and makes it effective.
04:mediator-from-above.christ: Christ goes down into the water first and the Spirit follows, "that he might sanctify, and the Spirit also sanctify" (Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 1.5.18).
where: Tertullian, *Bapt.* 4 — “an underlying material substance should catch the quality of that which overhangs it”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 6 — “in the water, under (the witness of) the angel, we are cleansed, and prepared for the Holy Spirit.”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 5.26 — “When the Holy Spirit also speaks, Who came down in the likeness of a dove?”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 2.5.14 (on the dove) — “That unbelievers might be called to belief.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.14 — “the Holy Ghost cometh down on thee also, and a Father's voice sounds over thee from on high”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.69 — “that He might bring the Spirit from above, and exalt man to heaven”

04:voice-from-heaven.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:voice-from-heaven.label: The Father's voice over the water
04:voice-from-heaven.def: A voice from heaven over the waters naming the Son.
04:voice-from-heaven.christ: Christ is the Son by nature. The baptized are sons "by adoption" (Cyril, *Cat.* 3.14).
where: Cyril, *Cat.* 3.14 — “a Father's voice sounds over thee from on high--not, "This is My Son," but, "This has now been made My son;"”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 5.26 — “the Father clearly calls from heaven in the Gospel narrative”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 1.5.19 — “Also God the Father spake from heaven. Thou hast the presence of the Trinity.”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.409 — “"The voice of the Lord is upon the waters, the voice of the Lord in majesty."”

04:fire-from-water.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:fire-from-water.label: Fire kindled on drenched wood
04:fire-from-water.def: Water is poured three times on the sacrifice and fire falls from heaven and kindles it.
04:fire-from-water.christ: Gregory reads it as faith in the Trinity and as the Spirit given in baptism. Cyril calls Christ the one “that baptizeth with the Holy Ghost and with fire” (*Cat.* 3.9).
where: Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.350 — “the fire was kindled by water thrice poured upon it”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.351 — “where the mystic water is, there is the kindling, warm, and fiery Spirit, that burns up the ungodly, and illuminates the faithful.”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 5.26 — “when Elijah prayed, fire was sent forth and consecrated the sacrifice.”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 5.27 — “To those [of old] a visible fire was sent that they might believe; for us who believe, the Lord works invisibly”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 10 — “true and stable faith is baptized with water, unto salvation; pretended and weak faith is baptized with fire, unto judgment.”

04:forerunner.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:forerunner.label: The one who prepares the way
04:forerunner.def: The servant who goes ahead, prepares by repentance and water, and points to the one greater who perfects.
04:forerunner.christ: John prepares for Christ, who baptizes "in the Spirit and fire" (Tertullian, *Bapt.* 10).
where: Tertullian, *Bapt.* 6 — “In this case also a type has preceded; for thus was John beforehand the Lord's forerunner”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 10 — “it conveyed nothing celestial, but it fore-ministered to things celestial”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 10 — “he who "prepares" does not himself "perfect," but procures for another to perfect.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.6 — “Baptism is the end of the Old Testament, and beginning of the New.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.6 — “The end he was of the Prophets”

04:anointed-one.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:anointed-one.label: The washed-then-anointed priest and king
04:anointed-one.def: One washed in water and then anointed with oil to be priest or king; the name "Christ" comes from this.
04:anointed-one.christ: Christ is anointed with the Spirit, not with material oil (Cyril, *Myst.* 3.2). The baptized become "christs" by sharing in His anointing.
where: Tertullian, *Bapt.* 7 — “Whence Aaron is called "Christ," from the "chrism," which is "the unction;"”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 7 — “the unction runs carnally, (i.e. on the body,) but profits spiritually”
Cyril, *Myst.* 3.6 — “Aaron was called Christ or Anointed, evidently from the typical Chrism.”
Cyril, *Myst.* 3.6 — “in advancing Solomon to the kingdom, anointed him after he had bathed in Gihon”
Cyril, *Myst.* 3.1 — “Now ye have been made Christs, by receiving the antitype of the Holy Ghost”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.5 — “for Aaron first washed, then was made high-priest”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 6.29 — “"Like the ointment upon the head, which went down to the beard, even Aaron's beard"”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 6.30 — “we are all anointed with spiritual grace for a share in the kingdom of God and in the priesthood.”

04:priest-king-with-bread.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:priest-king-with-bread.label: Melchizedek
04:priest-king-with-bread.def: A priest-king with no recorded beginning or end who brings out bread and wine to the victor.
04:priest-king-with-bread.christ: Melchizedek is Christ Himself: "Do you recognize Who that is?" (Ambrose, *De Myst.* 8.46).
where: Ambrose, *De Myst.* 8.45 — “Melchisedech, who is introduced without father, without mother, having neither beginning of days, nor ending, but like the Son of God”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 8.46 — “Can a man be king of righteousness, when himself he can hardly be righteous?”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 4.3.10 — “Melchizedek. He, then, is the author of the sacraments.”

04:manna.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:manna.label: Bread from heaven
04:manna.def: Food rained from heaven in the wilderness; a shadow of the living bread that does not die.
04:manna.christ: Christ's Body is the living bread (Ambrose, *De Myst.* 8.47).
where: Ambrose, *De Myst.* 8.47 — “But yet all those who ate that food died in the wilderness”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 8.49a — “That manna came from heaven, this is above the heavens”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 8.49b — “light is better than shadow, truth than a figure, the Body of its Giver than the manna from heaven.”
Cyril, *Myst.* 4.5 — “in the New Testament there is Bread of heaven, and a Cup of salvation”

04:jonah-descent.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:jonah-descent.label: Swallowed and cast up
04:jonah-descent.def: A prophet sleeps in a storm → is thrown into the sea → is swallowed by the monster → prays from Hades → is cast up on the third day → the nations repent.
04:jonah-descent.christ: Jonah is the type of Christ's descent into Hades and His rising on the third day (Cyril). In Irenaeus, Jonah is also every person swallowed by the devil and given back.
where: Cyril, *Cat.* 14.17 — “Jonas was asleep in the ship, and snoring amidst the stormy sea; while Jesus also slept”
Cyril, *Cat.* 14.17 — “The one was cast into a whale's belly: but the other of His own accord went down thither, where the invisible whale of death is.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 14.20 — “I know, he says, that I am a type of Him, who is to be laid in the Sepulchre hewn out of the rock.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 14.20 — “though in the whale, he says that he is in Hades; for he was a type of Christ, who was to descend into Hades.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 4.12 — “Did Jonah come forth from the whale on the third day, and hath not Christ then risen from the earth on the third day?”
Irenaeus, *AH* 3.20.1 — “did God permit man to be swallowed up by the great whale, who was the author of transgression”

04:three-third-day.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:three-third-day.label: Three / the third day
04:three-third-day.def: Three days (and three nights), three immersions, three pourings: the number of burial and resurrection.
04:three-third-day.christ: These are Christ's three days in the earth. The three immersions are also tied to the three Names (Gregory; Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 2.7.20–22).
where: Cyril, *Myst.* 2.4 — “descended three times into the water, and ascended again; here also hinting by a symbol at the three days burial of Christ.”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.199 — “by doing this thrice we represent for ourselves that grace of the Resurrection which was wrought in three days”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 2.7.20 — “that the triple confession might absolve the manifold fall of thy former life.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 4.12 — “Did Jonah come forth from the whale on the third day”
Augustine, *DDC* 3.35.50 — “we cannot make out the three days and three nights during which He foretold that He would be in the heart of the earth”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.350 — “the fire was kindled by water thrice poured upon it”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 6 — “wherever there are three, (that is, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, ) there is the Church”

04:forty.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:forty.label: Forty
04:forty.def: The number of fasting and testing (Moses, Elijah, Christ; Israel's years), read as life in time abstaining for eternity.
04:forty.christ: Christ's forty-day fast fulfils Moses and Elijah and reverses Israel's forty years (Tertullian, *Bapt.* 20).
where: Augustine, *DDC* 2.16.25 — “Moses and Elijah, and our Lord Himself, all fasted for forty days.”
Augustine, *DDC* 2.16.25 — “the number contains ten four times, indicating the knowledge of all things, and that knowledge interwoven with time.”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 20 — “the people, after crossing the sea, and being carried about in the desert during forty years”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 20 — “by maintaining a fast of forty days, that the man of God lives "not by bread alone,"”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.13 — “For as after His Baptism He was tempted forty days”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.21.2 — “Fasting forty days, like Moses and Elias, He afterwards hungered”
Irenaeus, *AH* 3.22.2 — “fasting those forty days, like Moses and Elias”

04:twelve.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:twelve.label: Twelve
04:twelve.def: A "legitimate" number standing for a whole; the twelve stones of the Jordan and the twelve apostles.
04:twelve.christ: The twelve are Christ's apostles, "the ministers of Baptism" (Gregory).
where: Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.325 — “Joshua also, who set up the twelve stones in the stream, was anticipating the coming of the twelve disciples, the ministers of Baptism.”
Augustine, *DDC* 3.35.51 — “our author calls those numbers legitimate which Holy Scripture more highly favors such as seven, or ten, or twelve”

04:seven.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:seven.label: Seven
04:seven.def: A "legitimate" number put for universal time or completeness; Naaman's seven dips.
04:seven.christ: Ambrose sets the seven dips "under the law" against baptism in the Trinity.
where: Augustine, *DDC* 3.35.51 — “"Seven times in the day do I praise Thee," means just the same as "His praise shall continually be in my mouth."”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 4.21 — “So that Syrian dipped himself seven times under the law, but you were baptized in the Name of the Trinity”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 3.16 — “he bade him dip himself seven times in the river Jordan.”

04:sixth-day.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:sixth-day.label: The sixth day (day of making and of dying)
04:sixth-day.def: The sixth day of creation, on which man was made and (Irenaeus argues) Adam died and Christ suffered.
04:sixth-day.christ: Christ "recapitulating in Himself this day" suffers on it, granting "a second creation" (Irenaeus, *AH* 5.23.2).
where: Irenaeus, *AH* 5.23.2 — “upon the day preceding the Sabbath, that is, the sixth day of the creation, on which day man was created”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.23.2 — “the Lord suffered death, in obedience to His Father, upon that day on which Adam died while he disobeyed God.”

04:first-and-last-adam.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:first-and-last-adam.label: Adam and the second Adam
04:first-and-last-adam.def: The first man, whose disobedience brought death, and Christ, the second, who replays and reverses his story.
04:first-and-last-adam.christ: Christ is the second Adam, made from virgin "earth" (Mary) to keep the analogy (Irenaeus, *AH* 3.21.10).
where: Irenaeus, *AH* 3.18.7 — “as by the disobedience of the one man who was originally moulded from virgin soil, the many were made sinners”
Irenaeus, *AH* 3.21.10 — “recapitulating Adam in Himself, rightly receive a birth, enabling Him to gather up Adam [into Himself], from Mary, who was as yet a virgin.”
Irenaeus, *AH* 3.22.3 — “Hence also was Adam himself termed by Paul "the figure of Him that was to come,"”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.16.3 — “In the second Adam, however, we are reconciled, being made obedient even unto death.”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.21.1 — “as our species went down to death through a vanquished man, so we may ascend to life again through a victorious one”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.31 — “Very speedily I passed sentence upon Adam, very speedily I pardon thee.”
Cyril, *Myst.* 2.2 — “ye bore the likeness of the first-formed Adam, who was naked in the garden, and was not ashamed.”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 5.3.14 — “Thou becamest a dry tree in Adam; but now through the grace of Christ thou hast budded into a fruitful tree.”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.504 — “No longer shall Adam be confounded when called by Thee, nor hide himself”

04:eve-and-mary.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:eve-and-mary.label: The virgin who disobeyed and the virgin who obeyed
04:eve-and-mary.def: Two betrothed virgins who each receive an angel's word: Eve disobeys and brings death; Mary obeys and brings life.
04:eve-and-mary.christ: Mary's obedience opens the way for the birth of the second Adam. The woman's seed watches for the serpent's head (Irenaeus, *AH* 5.21.1).
where: Irenaeus, *AH* 3.22.4 — “Mary the Virgin is found obedient” ... “But Eve was disobedient; for she did not obey when as yet she was a virgin.”
Irenaeus, *AH* 3.22.4 — “the knot of Eve's disobedience was loosed by the obedience of Mary.”
Irenaeus, *AH* 3.22.4 — “indicating the back-reference from Mary to Eve”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.19.1 — “as the human race fell into bondage to death by means of a virgin, so is it rescued by a virgin”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.19.1 — “in order that the Virgin Mary might become the patroness (advocata) of the virgin Eve.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 12.15 — “Through Eve yet virgin came death; through a virgin, or rather from a virgin, must the Life appear”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 5.1.4 — “guilt through woman, grace through the Lord Jesus Christ.”

04:serpent.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:serpent.label: Serpent
04:serpent.def: The deceiver in the garden whose head the woman's seed watches; but also, in a good sense, an image of wise self-renewal.
04:serpent.christ: Christ crushes the serpent's head (Irenaeus). In the bronze serpent the sign of death becomes the sign of the crucified (Cyril, *Cat.* 13.20).
where: Irenaeus, *AH* 5.21.1 — “was preached as keeping watch for the head of the serpent.”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.19.1 — “the coming of the serpent is conquered by the harmlessness of the dove”
Cyril, *Myst.* 1.4 — “"I renounce thee,"--thou crafty and most subtle serpent.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.7 — “For every serpent creeps into a hole and casts its old slough, and having rubbed off the old skin, grows young again in body.”
Augustine, *DDC* 2.16.24 — “the serpent gets rid of its old skin by squeezing itself through a narrow hole, and thus acquires new strength”
Augustine, *DDC* 3.25.36 — “the serpent is used in a good sense, "Be wise as serpents;" and again, in a bad sense”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.76 — “drew along his serpent train, a disguise worthy of his own intent”

04:recapitulative-reversal.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:recapitulative-reversal.label: Undoing by the same steps
04:recapitulative-reversal.def: The fall is undone by repeating its steps in reverse: virgin, tree, garden, evening, day, side. Each instrument of loss becomes an instrument of salvation.
04:recapitulative-reversal.christ: This is Irenaeus' "recapitulation": Christ sums up Adam in Himself and goes through each step again, the other way.
where: Irenaeus, *AH* 3.22.4 — “what is joined together could not otherwise be put asunder than by inversion of the process by which these bonds of union had arisen”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.16.3 — “so was it also by these same that He brought in obedience”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.19.1 — “virginal disobedience having been balanced in the opposite scale by virginal obedience.”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.21.1 — “He has therefore, in His work of recapitulation, summed up all things, both waging war against our enemy”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.23.2 — “by summing up in Himself the whole human race from the beginning to the end, He has also summed up its death.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 12.15 — “By the very same weapons, therefore, wherewith the Devil used to vanquish us, have we been saved.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.18 — “For this cause Jesus assumes the thorns, that He may cancel the sentence”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.19 — “I am truly astonished at the truth of the types. In Paradise was the Fall, and in a Garden was our Salvation.”
Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 5.1.4 — “Because whence the guilt, thence the grace”

04:garden.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:garden.label: Paradise / garden
04:garden.def: The garden toward the east where man fell, which is reopened through the cross and baptism; read as the Church.
04:garden.christ: Christ is buried in a garden and opens Paradise to the robber (Cyril, *Cat.* 13.19, 13.31).
where: Cyril, *Cat.* 13.19 — “In Paradise was the Fall, and in a Garden was our Salvation.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.31 — “thou by the Tree art brought into Paradise.”
Cyril, *Myst.* 1.9 — “there is opened to thee the paradise of God, which He planted towards the East, whence for his transgression our first father was banished”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.499 — “Thou didst banish us from Paradise, and didst recall us”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.505 — “Nor shall the flaming sword encircle Paradise around”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.20.2 — “the Church has been planted as a garden (paradisus) in this world”
Irenaeus, *AH* 5.20.2 — “Eat ye from every Scripture of the Lord”

04:fig-tree.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:fig-tree.label: Fig leaves and the cursed fig tree
04:fig-tree.def: Fig leaves were the first covering of shame; Christ curses a fig tree with leaves but no fruit, cancelling that sign.
04:fig-tree.christ: Christ cancels the curse represented by the leaves (Cyril).
where: Cyril, *Cat.* 13.18 — “At the time of the sin, they clothed themselves with fig-leaves; for this cause Jesus also made the fig-tree the last of His signs.”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.18 — “He curses the fig-tree, not every fig-tree, but that one alone, for the sake of the figure”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.500 — “Thou didst strip off the fig-tree leaves, an unseemly covering, and put upon us a costly garment”

04:thorns.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:thorns.label: Thorns
04:thorns.def: The curse on the ground ("thorns and thistles"), which Christ takes on Himself as a crown.
04:thorns.christ: The crown of thorns cancels the curse on the ground.
where: Cyril, *Cat.* 13.18 — “For this cause Jesus assumes the thorns, that He may cancel the sentence”
Cyril, *Cat.* 13.18 — “for this cause also was He buried in the earth, that the earth which had been cursed might receive the blessing instead of a curse.”

04:garment.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:garment.label: Stripping off and putting on
04:garment.def: The old garment (old man, fig leaves, filthy rags) taken off at baptism; a white or costly garment put on.
04:garment.christ: Christ is the garment put on (Cyril, *Myst.* 1.10; Gal 3:27). His nakedness on the cross strips the powers (Cyril, *Myst.* 2.2).
where: Cyril, *Myst.* 2.2 — “this was an image of putting off the old man with his deeds”
Cyril, *Myst.* 2.2 — “imitating Christ, who was stripped naked on the Cross”
Cyril, *Myst.* 2.2 — “ye bore the likeness of the first-formed Adam, who was naked in the garden, and was not ashamed.”
Cyril, *Myst.* 4.8 — “having put off thy old garments, and put on those which are spiritually white”
Cyril, *Myst.* 1.10 — “clothed in the garment of salvation, even Jesus Christ.”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.376 — “putting off our sins like some poor and patched garment, are clothed in the holy and most fair garment of regeneration.”
Gregory, *Bapt. Chr.*, l.500 — “Thou didst strip off the fig-tree leaves, an unseemly covering, and put upon us a costly garment”
Tertullian, *Bapt.* 13 — “the clothing, in some sense, of the faith which before was bare”
Cyril, *Cat.* 3.7 — “Put off the old man with his doings”

04:west-to-east.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:west-to-east.label: Turning from west to east
04:west-to-east.def: West is the region of darkness and the devil; east is the region of light and Paradise; conversion is a turn from one to the other.
04:west-to-east.christ: To turn east is to turn to Christ (Ambrose).
where: Cyril, *Myst.* 1.4 — “Since the West is the region of sensible darkness, and he being darkness has his dominion also in darkness”
Cyril, *Myst.* 1.9 — “a symbol of this was thy turning from West to East, the place of light.”
Ambrose, *De Myst.* 2.7 — “then you turned to the east; for he who renounces the devil turns to Christ, and beholds Him face to face.”

04:darkness-to-light.work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
04:darkness-to-light.label: Night to day
04:darkness-to-light.def: Movement from darkness or night to light or day, enacted in the descent and ascent of baptism.
04:darkness-to-light.christ: Christ is the pillar of light (Ambrose, *De Sacr.* 1.6.22).
where: Cyril, *Myst.* 2.4 — “in the descent, as in the night, ye saw nothing, but in ascending again ye were as in the day.”
